title: The Symmetric Perceptron: a Teacher-Student Scenario
summary: We introduce and solve a teacher-student formulation of the symmetric binary Perceptron, turning a traditionally storage-oriented model into a planted inference problem with a guaranteed solution at any sample density. We adapt the formulation of the symmetric Perceptron which traditionally considers either the u-shaped potential or the rectangular one, by including labels in both regions. With this formulation, we analyze both the Bayes-optimal regime at for noise-less examples and the effect of thermal noise under two different potential/classification rules. Using annealed and quenched free-entropy calculations in the high-dimensional limit, we map the phase diagram in the three control parameters, namely the sample density $α$, the distance between the origin and one of the symmetric hyperplanes $κ$ and temperature $T$, and identify a robust scenario where learning is organized by a second-order instability that creates teacher-correlated suboptimal states, followed by a first-order transition to full alignment. We show how this structure depends on the choice of potential, the interplay between metastability of the suboptimal solution and its melting towards the planted configuration, which is relevant for Monte Carlo-based optimization algorithms.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a teacher-student formulation of the symmetric binary Perceptron, transforming it from a storage problem to a planted inference problem with guaranteed solutions at any sample density, and analyzes phase transitions in learning dynamics.
AI.motivation: To reformulate the symmetric binary Perceptron from a traditional storage-oriented model into a planted inference problem with guaranteed solutions, enabling analysis of learning dynamics and phase transitions in high-dimensional settings.
AI.method: Adapts symmetric Perceptron formulation with labels in both regions, analyzes Bayes-optimal regime for noise-less examples and thermal noise effects under different potentials/classification rules using annealed and quenched free-entropy calculations in high-dimensional limit.
AI.result: Maps phase diagram in three control parameters (sample density α, distance κ, temperature T), identifies robust scenario with second-order instability creating teacher-correlated suboptimal states followed by first-order transition to full alignment, shows dependence on potential choice and interplay between metastability and melting.
AI.conclusion: The teacher-student formulation reveals structured learning dynamics with distinct phase transitions, providing insights into optimization algorithms and the relationship between metastable states and convergence to planted configurations in high-dimensional inference problems.

title: Krylov-space anatomy and spread complexity of a disordered quantum spin chain
summary: We investigate the anatomy and complexity of quantum states in Krylov space, in the ergodic and many-body localised (MBL) phases of a disordered, interacting spin chain. The Krylov basis generated by the Hamiltonian from an initial state provides a representation in which the spread of the time-evolving state constitutes a basis-optimised measure of complexity. We show that the long-time Krylov spread complexity sharply distinguishes the two phases. In the ergodic phase, the infinite-time complexity scales linearly with the Fock-space dimension, indicating that the state spreads over a finite fraction of the Krylov chain. By contrast, it grows sublinearly in the MBL phase, implying that the long-time state occupies only a vanishing fraction of the chain. Further, the profile of the infinite-time state along the Krylov chain exhibits a stretched-exponential decay in the MBL phase. This behaviour reflects a broad distribution of decay lengthscales, associated with different eigenstates contributing to the long-time state. Consistently, a large-deviation analysis of the statistics of eigenstate spread complexities shows that while the ergodic phase receives contributions from almost all eigenstates, the complexity in the MBL phase is dominated by a vanishing fraction of eigenstates, which have anomalously large complexity relative to the typical ones.

AI.tldr: Krylov spread complexity distinguishes ergodic and MBL phases: linear scaling with Fock-space dimension in ergodic phase vs. sublinear in MBL phase, with stretched-exponential decay profiles in MBL.
AI.motivation: To investigate quantum state complexity in Krylov space as a diagnostic tool for distinguishing ergodic and many-body localized (MBL) phases in disordered, interacting spin chains.
AI.method: Analyze Krylov basis generated by Hamiltonian from initial state, using spread complexity as basis-optimised measure; examine long-time Krylov spread complexity scaling, infinite-time state profiles, and large-deviation analysis of eigenstate spread complexities.
AI.result: Long-time Krylov spread complexity sharply distinguishes phases: linear scaling with Fock-space dimension in ergodic phase (state spreads over finite fraction of Krylov chain) vs. sublinear in MBL phase (vanishing fraction). MBL phase shows stretched-exponential decay profile along Krylov chain with broad distribution of decay lengthscales. Large-deviation analysis reveals ergodic phase contributions from almost all eigenstates, while MBL complexity dominated by vanishing fraction of eigenstates with anomalously large complexity.
AI.conclusion: Krylov spread complexity serves as effective diagnostic for ergodic-MBL phase distinction, revealing fundamentally different complexity scaling and eigenstate contributions between phases, with MBL showing localized complexity dominated by rare eigenstates.

title: The Born Rule as the Unique Refinement-Stable Induced Weight on Robust Record Sectors
comment: Quantum foundations. Distinct conditional uniqueness theorem for induced weight on robust record sectors
summary: This paper proves a conditional structural uniqueness theorem for induced weight on robust record sectors within an admissible Hilbert record layer. Its theorem target and additive carrier differ from those of the standard Born-rule routes: additivity is not placed on the full projector lattice, but on disjoint admissible continuation bundles through an extensive bundle valuation, from which the sector-level additive law is inherited under admissible refinement. Accordingly, the result is not a Gleason-type representation theorem in different language, but a distinct uniqueness theorem about induced sector weight inherited from bundle additivity on admissible continuation structure. Under two explicit structural conditions, internal equivalence of admissible binary refinement profiles and sufficient admissible refinement richness, the quadratic assignment is the only non-negative refinement-stable induced weight on robust record sectors. In the main theorem, refinement richness is secured by admissible binary saturation. A supplementary proposition shows that dense admissible saturation already suffices if continuity of the profile function is added. Under normalization, the result reduces to the standard Born assignment.

AI.tldr: Proves conditional uniqueness theorem for induced weight on robust record sectors, showing Born rule is unique under structural conditions of equivalence and refinement richness.
AI.motivation: To establish a distinct uniqueness theorem for induced sector weight that differs from standard Gleason-type representation theorems, focusing on weight inherited from bundle additivity on admissible continuation structure rather than full projector lattice additivity.
AI.method: Uses extensive bundle valuation on disjoint admissible continuation bundles, from which sector-level additive law is inherited under admissible refinement. Employs two structural conditions: internal equivalence of admissible binary refinement profiles and sufficient admissible refinement richness (secured by admissible binary saturation).
AI.result: Under specified structural conditions, the quadratic assignment (Born rule) is the only non-negative refinement-stable induced weight on robust record sectors. With normalization, this reduces to standard Born assignment.
AI.conclusion: Provides a conditional structural uniqueness theorem that establishes Born rule as unique under conditions of equivalence and refinement richness, offering a distinct approach from standard Gleason-type theorems by focusing on bundle-level additivity inherited to sectors.

title: Implementing non-Abelian Hatano-Nelson model in electric circuits
summary: Non-Hermitian systems generally host complex spectra that bring unique spectral topologies, leading to the spectral braiding and non-Hermitian skin effect. The experimental exploration of non-Hermitian physics is mainly concentrated in artificial systems due to the flexibility in the introduction of the non-Hermiticity, but to date has focused only on the systems without gauge fields or with Abelian gauge fields. Here, we propose a non-Abelian Hatano-Nelson model with a nonreciprocal U(2) gauge field. The gauge field induces two non-Hermitian phenomena: the first is the Hopf-link-shaped complex energy braiding, and the second is the bipolar skin effect arising under the non-Abelian condition. The non-Abelian Hatano-Nelson model is implemented in electric circuits, and the Hopf-link-shaped admittance spectra and bipolar skin admittance modes are observed. Our work enriches the experimental non-Hermitian physics, and provides an approach to designing multifunctional non-Hermitian devices.

AI.tldr: Experimental demonstration of non-Abelian Hatano-Nelson model in electric circuits showing Hopf-link energy braiding and bipolar skin effect induced by nonreciprocal U(2) gauge field.
AI.motivation: Previous experimental non-Hermitian physics has been limited to systems without gauge fields or with Abelian gauge fields, lacking exploration of non-Abelian gauge fields in non-Hermitian systems.
AI.method: Proposed a non-Abelian Hatano-Nelson model with nonreciprocal U(2) gauge field and implemented it experimentally using electric circuits to measure admittance spectra and skin modes.
AI.result: Observed Hopf-link-shaped complex energy braiding in admittance spectra and bipolar skin admittance modes, demonstrating two distinct non-Hermitian phenomena induced by the non-Abelian gauge field.
AI.conclusion: Enriches experimental non-Hermitian physics by introducing non-Abelian gauge fields and provides a design approach for multifunctional non-Hermitian devices.

title: Spectral methods: crucial for machine learning, natural for quantum computers?
summary: This article presents an argument for why quantum computers could unlock new methods for machine learning. We argue that spectral methods, in particular those that learn, regularise, or otherwise manipulate the Fourier spectrum of a machine learning model, are often natural for quantum computers. For example, if a generative machine learning model is represented by a quantum state, the Quantum Fourier Transform allows us to manipulate the Fourier spectrum of the state using the entire toolbox of quantum routines, an operation that is usually prohibitive for classical models. At the same time, spectral methods are surprisingly fundamental to machine learning: A spectral bias has recently been hypothesised to be the core principle behind the success of deep learning; support vector machines have been known for decades to regularise in Fourier space, and convolutional neural nets build filters in the Fourier space of images. Could, then, quantum computing open fundamentally different, much more direct and resource-efficient ways to design the spectral properties of a model? We discuss this potential in detail here, hoping to stimulate a direction in quantum machine learning research that puts the question of ``why quantum?'' first.

AI.tldr: Quantum computers could enable new machine learning approaches by naturally manipulating Fourier spectra of models, potentially offering more direct and efficient spectral design than classical methods.
AI.motivation: The paper argues that quantum computers are naturally suited for spectral methods in machine learning, which are fundamental to many successful ML approaches. It questions whether quantum computing could provide fundamentally different, more direct, and resource-efficient ways to design spectral properties of models compared to classical methods.
AI.method: The paper presents a conceptual argument and analysis rather than a specific experimental method. It examines how quantum computers could manipulate Fourier spectra of machine learning models using quantum routines like the Quantum Fourier Transform, particularly when models are represented as quantum states.
AI.result: The analysis suggests that quantum computers could potentially unlock new methods for machine learning by enabling efficient manipulation of Fourier spectra, which is often prohibitive for classical models. This could lead to more direct control over spectral properties that are fundamental to ML success.
AI.conclusion: Quantum computing may open fundamentally different approaches to designing spectral properties of machine learning models. The paper advocates for a research direction in quantum machine learning that prioritizes the question of "why quantum?" and explores the potential advantages of quantum spectral methods.

title: A versatile neural-network toolbox for testing Bell locality in networks
comment: 10+4 pages, 4+3 figures, RevTeX 4.2. The computational appendix is available at https://www.github.com/Antoine0Girardin/local_model_in_networks
summary: Determining whether an observed distribution of events generated in a quantum network is Bell local, i.e., if it admits an alternative realization in terms of independent local variables, is extremely challenging. Building upon arXiv:1907.10552, we develop a software solution that parameterizes local models in networks via neural networks. This allows one to leverage optimization tools available from the machine learning community in the search of network Bell nonlocality. Our solution applies to arbitrary networks, is easy to use, and includes technical improvements that significantly increase performance compared to previous implementations. We apply it to investigate nonlocality in several networks hitherto unexplored, providing insights on the corresponding quantum nonlocal sets and suggesting concrete, promising realizations of quantum nonlocal correlations.

AI.tldr: Neural network-based software for detecting Bell nonlocality in quantum networks, applicable to arbitrary topologies with improved performance over previous methods.
AI.motivation: Determining Bell locality in quantum networks is extremely challenging, requiring efficient computational methods to analyze observed event distributions for alternative local variable realizations.
AI.method: Parameterizes local models in networks via neural networks, leveraging machine learning optimization tools to search for network Bell nonlocality. Builds upon arXiv:1907.10552 with technical improvements for better performance.
AI.result: Developed software solution applicable to arbitrary networks, easy to use, with significantly increased performance compared to previous implementations. Applied to investigate nonlocality in several previously unexplored networks.
AI.conclusion: Provides insights on quantum nonlocal sets and suggests concrete, promising realizations of quantum nonlocal correlations through neural network-based analysis of network Bell nonlocality.

title: Inequality for Strong-Weak Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking in Fermionic Open Quantum systems
summary: Under decoherence, an initial Gaussian (free-fermion) state evolves into a non-Gaussian mixed state, so the resulting decohered fermionic state is not exactly solvable in general. We show through an inequality that a class of Rényi-2 correlators of the decohered fermion state are upper-bounded by the Rényi-2 correlator serving as a proximate diagnostic of strong-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) of the charge-U(1) symmetry. This inequality holds for arbitrary decoherence strength and suggests that decoherence drives fermionic quantum matter toward U(1) SW-SSB. We also make connections between our inequality and other subjects such as projected quantum spin Hall insulator and Dirac spin liquid states.

AI.tldr: Decoherence in fermionic systems leads to non-Gaussian states, but Rényi-2 correlators of decohered states are bounded by a diagnostic for U(1) strong-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking, suggesting decoherence drives toward SW-SSB.
AI.motivation: To understand how decoherence affects fermionic quantum matter, particularly when initial Gaussian states evolve into non-Gaussian mixed states that are generally not exactly solvable, and to find diagnostic tools for analyzing symmetry breaking under decoherence.
AI.method: Develop an inequality showing that Rényi-2 correlators of decohered fermion states are upper-bounded by the Rényi-2 correlator that serves as a diagnostic for U(1) strong-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB). The analysis holds for arbitrary decoherence strength and connects to specific physical systems.
AI.result: The inequality demonstrates that decoherence drives fermionic quantum matter toward U(1) SW-SSB, regardless of decoherence strength. Connections are established to projected quantum spin Hall insulator and Dirac spin liquid states, showing broader applicability of the theoretical framework.
AI.conclusion: Decoherence in fermionic systems universally promotes U(1) strong-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking, as evidenced by the bounding inequality for Rényi-2 correlators, providing insights into decoherence effects on symmetry breaking and connections to various quantum matter states.

title: Multipartite entanglement dynamics in quantum walks
summary: Quantum walks constitute a rich area of quantum information science, where multipartite entanglement plays a central role in the dynamics and scalability of quantum advantage over classical simulators. In this work, we study the multipartite entanglement of quantum walks in optical settings. We present methods for computing a geometric measure of entanglement for arbitrary partitions of a single-walker quantum walk and for analyzing the entanglement in multi-walker scenarios. These techniques are used for numerical studies on the entanglement dynamics of quantum walks in large systems and under various initial conditions. For a given bipartition, based on the coin degrees of freedom, we derive exact expressions describing the complete entanglement dynamics for arbitrary localized initial conditions. We use these expressions for analytic statements about the asymptotic behavior of the system. Furthermore, we demonstrate the emergence of entanglement typicality in statistical ensembles of random optical networks.

AI.tldr: The paper develops methods to compute and analyze multipartite entanglement in quantum walks, deriving exact expressions for entanglement dynamics and demonstrating entanglement typicality in random optical networks.
AI.motivation: Multipartite entanglement is crucial for quantum walks' dynamics and scalability advantages over classical simulators, particularly in optical settings where understanding entanglement properties is essential for quantum information applications.
AI.method: Developed methods for computing geometric measures of entanglement for arbitrary partitions in single-walker quantum walks and analyzing entanglement in multi-walker scenarios. Derived exact expressions for complete entanglement dynamics based on coin degrees of freedom for arbitrary localized initial conditions.
AI.result: Numerical studies on entanglement dynamics in large systems under various initial conditions. Analytic statements about asymptotic behavior using derived exact expressions. Demonstration of entanglement typicality emergence in statistical ensembles of random optical networks.
AI.conclusion: The work provides comprehensive tools for analyzing multipartite entanglement in quantum walks, enabling detailed study of entanglement dynamics and statistical properties in optical quantum walk implementations.

title: Phased outcome-complete simulation
summary: We generalize the polynomial-time outcome-complete simulation algorithm for stabilizer circuits in arXiv:2309.08676 to track global phases exactly, yielding what we call phased outcome-complete simulation. The original algorithm enabled equivalence checking of stabilizer circuits with intermediate measurements and conditional Pauli corrections for all input states and all measurement outcomes simultaneously, but it tracked quantum states only up to a global phase. Our generalization removes this limitation and enables equivalence checking for an important family of non-stabilizer circuits: stabilizer circuits augmented with single-qubit rotations $\exp(iαZ)$ by symbolic angles. Two such circuits are equivalent if they implement the same quantum channel for all values of the symbolic angles and all measurement outcomes, given a one-to-one correspondence between rotation angles in the two circuits and a mapping between measurement outcomes. This model enables testing of compilation algorithms that transform the Clifford portions of a computation while preserving rotation angles. Examples include Pauli-based computation, edge-disjoint path compilation for surface codes, and custom compilation strategies for reversible circuits such as adders, multipliers, and table lookups. Our efficient classical verification methods extend naturally to circuits with outcome-parity-conditional Pauli gates and intermediate measurements, features that are ubiquitous in fault-tolerant quantum computing but are rarely addressed by existing equivalence-checking approaches.

AI.tldr: Extends stabilizer circuit simulation to track global phases exactly, enabling equivalence checking for circuits with symbolic-angle rotations and measurement-dependent operations.
AI.motivation: Existing stabilizer circuit simulation algorithms track quantum states only up to global phase, limiting their ability to verify equivalence for circuits containing non-stabilizer operations like symbolic-angle rotations. There's a need for verification methods that handle features common in fault-tolerant quantum computing like measurement-dependent Pauli corrections.
AI.method: Generalizes polynomial-time outcome-complete simulation algorithm to track global phases exactly, creating phased outcome-complete simulation. This enables equivalence checking for stabilizer circuits augmented with single-qubit rotations exp(iαZ) by symbolic angles, handling all measurement outcomes and input states simultaneously while preserving phase information.
AI.result: Develops efficient classical verification methods for circuits with symbolic-angle rotations, outcome-parity-conditional Pauli gates, and intermediate measurements. The approach can verify equivalence of circuits that implement the same quantum channel for all values of symbolic angles and all measurement outcomes.
AI.conclusion: The phased outcome-complete simulation enables verification of compilation algorithms that transform Clifford portions while preserving rotation angles, applicable to Pauli-based computation, surface code compilation, and reversible circuit compilation strategies that are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Auto-regressive Neural Quantum State Sampling for Selected Configuration Interaction
summary: Accurate ground-state energy calculations remain a central challenge in quantum chemistry due to the exponential scaling of the many-body Hilbert space. Variational Monte Carlo and variational quantum eigensolvers offer promising ansatz optimization approaches but face limitations in convergence as well as hardware constraints. We introduce a particular Selected Configuration Interaction (SCI) algorithm that uses auto-regressive neural networks (ARNNs) to guide subspace expansion for ground-state search. Leveraging the unique properties of ARNNs, our algorithm efficiently constructs compact variational subspaces from learned ground-state statistics, which in turn accelerates convergence to the ground-state energy. Benchmarks on molecular systems demonstrate that ARNN-guided subspace expansion combines the strengths of neural-network representations and classical subspace methods, providing a scalable framework for classical and hybrid quantum-classical algorithms.

AI.tldr: ARNN-guided Selected Configuration Interaction algorithm uses auto-regressive neural networks to efficiently construct compact variational subspaces for ground-state energy calculations, accelerating convergence in molecular systems.
AI.motivation: Accurate ground-state energy calculations in quantum chemistry face exponential scaling challenges. Variational Monte Carlo and variational quantum eigensolvers have limitations in convergence and hardware constraints, necessitating more efficient approaches.
AI.method: Introduces a Selected Configuration Interaction algorithm that uses auto-regressive neural networks to guide subspace expansion for ground-state search. ARNNs learn ground-state statistics to efficiently construct compact variational subspaces.
AI.result: Benchmarks on molecular systems demonstrate that ARNN-guided subspace expansion accelerates convergence to ground-state energy by combining neural-network representations with classical subspace methods.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a scalable framework for both classical and hybrid quantum-classical algorithms, leveraging the strengths of neural-network representations and classical subspace methods for efficient ground-state calculations.

title: Clifford synthesis via generalized S and CZ gates
summary: We show that any $n$-qubit Clifford unitary can be implemented using at most $2n$ multi-qubit joint measurements. All the multi-qubit joint measurements used for implementing the Clifford unitary can be chosen to form at most two sets of independent mutually-commuting measurements. Each of these sets is of size at most $n$. This enables very flexible space-time trade-offs when implementing Clifford unitaries. We also discuss a version of the result that relies on multi-target CNOTs and is more relevant for targeting fault-tolerant hardware based on Quantum LDPC codes.

AI.tldr: Any n-qubit Clifford unitary can be implemented using at most 2n multi-qubit joint measurements, organized into at most two sets of mutually-commuting measurements, enabling flexible space-time trade-offs.
AI.motivation: To develop efficient implementations of Clifford unitaries using joint measurements, enabling space-time trade-offs and providing methods relevant for fault-tolerant quantum computing with Quantum LDPC codes.
AI.method: Uses at most 2n multi-qubit joint measurements organized into at most two sets of independent mutually-commuting measurements, each of size at most n. Also discusses a version using multi-target CNOTs.
AI.result: Any n-qubit Clifford unitary can be implemented with at most 2n joint measurements, providing flexible space-time trade-offs and hardware-relevant implementations for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
AI.conclusion: The paper presents an efficient measurement-based approach to implementing Clifford unitaries with significant space-time flexibility, offering practical advantages for fault-tolerant quantum hardware based on Quantum LDPC codes.

title: Resource-optimal quantum mode parameter estimation with multimode Gaussian states
summary: Quantum mode parameter estimation determines parameters governing the shape of electromagnetic modes occupied by a quantum state of radiation. Canonical examples, time delays and frequency shifts, underpin radar, lidar, and optical clocks. A comprehensive framework recently established that broad families of quantum states can attain the Heisenberg limit, surpassing any classical strategy. This raises a fundamental question: among all quantum-enhanced strategies, which is truly optimal? Answering this requires identifying physically meaningful resources governing each estimation task, so quantum states can be compared on equal footing. We show these resources are connected to the eigenmode basis of the generator of the relevant mode transformation. For time-shift estimation, whose generator is diagonal in the frequency domain, the pertinent resources are the mean frequency and bandwidth; analogous quantities emerge for other transformations. Our framework unifies two historically separate perspectives: the particle-number aspect and the mode-structure of quantum light, providing a coherent picture of quantum-enhanced sensing with multimode radiation. Within this unified framework, we derive a tight upper bound on the quantum Fisher information for multimode Gaussian states, expressed in terms of these natural resources, and analytically identify the optimal Gaussian states saturating it. These optimal states take a particularly transparent form in the generator eigenbasis, a structural simplicity reflecting the deep connection between the geometry of the mode transformation and the architecture of the optimal probe. We further demonstrate that multimode homodyne detection constitutes the optimal measurement, achieving this bound and completing the end-to-end characterization of optimal quantum metrology strategies for mode parameter estimation.

AI.tldr: The paper develops a unified framework for optimal quantum metrology of mode parameters, identifying natural resources tied to transformation generators, deriving tight bounds for Gaussian states, and identifying optimal states and measurements.
AI.motivation: To determine truly optimal quantum-enhanced strategies for mode parameter estimation by identifying physically meaningful resources that allow fair comparison of quantum states, unifying particle-number and mode-structure perspectives.
AI.method: Develops framework connecting resources to eigenmode basis of transformation generators; derives tight upper bound on quantum Fisher information for multimode Gaussian states; analytically identifies optimal Gaussian states; demonstrates optimality of multimode homodyne detection.
AI.result: Shows resources are mean frequency and bandwidth for time-shift estimation; derives tight bound on quantum Fisher information for Gaussian states; identifies optimal Gaussian states with transparent structure in generator eigenbasis; proves multimode homodyne achieves bound.
AI.conclusion: Provides complete end-to-end characterization of optimal quantum metrology strategies for mode parameter estimation, unifying particle-number and mode-structure perspectives, with optimal states reflecting geometry of mode transformations.

title: Fluorescence spectrum of a hybrid three-level quantum dot nanoparticle system
summary: Quantum optics provides a fundamental framework for understanding the interaction between light and matter at the quantum level. Recently, it has been shown that under incoherent pumping, the resonance fluorescence spectrum dramatically changes. Engineering the resonance fluorescence spectrum paves the way towards solid-state-based single-photon sources. In this paper, we start by reviewing and reproducing some of the results concerning the resonance fluorescence spectrum, single-photon sources, dressed-state lasers, and luminescence spectrum of a quantum dot in a microcavity. Photon correlations in quantum optical systems and spectral properties of radiation emitted by atomic and semiconductor systems interacting with external fields are investigated. The well known Mollow triplet structure of the emission spectrum is discussed, together with the role of dressed states in explaining the origin of the three spectral peaks. Furthermore, the luminescence spectra of quantum emitters coupled to microcavities are reviewed. The numerical results presented here contribute to the theoretical understanding of resonance fluorescence, photon correlations, and engineered emission in quantum optical systems. These studies highlight the rich physical properties arising from light matter interaction at the quantum level and demonstrate their relevance for emerging quantum technologies.

AI.tldr: Review paper analyzing resonance fluorescence spectra, photon correlations, and engineered emission in quantum optical systems, with focus on Mollow triplet, dressed states, and applications to single-photon sources.
AI.motivation: To understand and engineer quantum light-matter interactions, particularly resonance fluorescence spectra under incoherent pumping, for developing solid-state single-photon sources and exploring rich physical phenomena in quantum optics.
AI.method: Theoretical review and numerical reproduction of existing results on resonance fluorescence spectra, dressed-state lasers, quantum dot luminescence in microcavities, and photon correlation analysis in quantum optical systems.
AI.result: Demonstrates dramatic changes in resonance fluorescence spectrum under incoherent pumping, explains Mollow triplet structure via dressed states, analyzes photon correlations, and reviews luminescence spectra of quantum emitters in microcavities.
AI.conclusion: The study contributes to theoretical understanding of engineered emission in quantum systems and highlights the relevance of these quantum optical phenomena for emerging quantum technologies like single-photon sources.

title: Coefficient-Decoupled Matrix Product Operators as an Interface to Linear-Combination-of-Unitaries Circuits
summary: We introduce a coefficient-decoupled matrix product operator (MPO) representation for Pauli-sum operators that separates reusable symbolic operator support from a tunable coefficient bridge across a fixed bipartition. This representation provides a direct interface to linear-combination-of-unitaries (LCU) circuits: the symbolic left/right dictionaries define a static \textsc{Select} oracle that is compiled once, while coefficient updates modify only a dynamic \textsc{Prep} oracle. As a proof of concept, we construct compact state-adapted Pauli pools by sampling Pauli strings from a pretrained matrix product state (MPS), pruning them to a fixed symbolic pool, optimizing only their coefficients, and transferring the resulting weights directly to the LCU interface. The resulting workflow provides a reusable classical-to-quantum compilation strategy in which the symbolic operator structure is compiled once, and subsequent updates are confined to a low-dimensional coefficient object.

AI.tldr: A coefficient-decoupled MPO representation separates Pauli-sum operators into reusable symbolic structure and tunable coefficients, enabling efficient LCU circuit compilation with static Select oracles and dynamic Prep updates.
AI.motivation: To create a more efficient compilation strategy for quantum circuits that separates the static symbolic structure of operators from tunable coefficients, enabling reusable classical-to-quantum compilation with minimal updates needed for coefficient changes.
AI.method: Introduces a coefficient-decoupled MPO representation for Pauli-sum operators that separates symbolic operator support from coefficient bridges. Uses this representation as direct interface to LCU circuits with static Select oracles (compiled once) and dynamic Prep oracles (updated for coefficient changes). Constructs compact state-adapted Pauli pools by sampling from pretrained MPS, pruning to fixed symbolic pool, optimizing coefficients, and transferring weights to LCU interface.
AI.result: Provides a reusable compilation workflow where symbolic operator structure is compiled once and subsequent updates are confined to low-dimensional coefficient objects, enabling efficient coefficient optimization without recompiling the entire quantum circuit structure.
AI.conclusion: The coefficient-decoupled MPO representation offers an efficient interface between classical optimization and quantum compilation, enabling reusable symbolic structures with dynamic coefficient updates for LCU-based quantum algorithms.

title: Modeling Quantum Billiards with the Finite Element Method: Searching for Quantum Scarring Candidates
summary: An electron in quantum confinement takes on a discrete energy spectrum which is defined based on the solution to the Schrodinger Equation for a given potential. Well defined closed-form energy spectra are known for the particle in a box, circular potential, quarter circle potential, and an equilateral triangle. A closed-form solution for more complex shapes may not be known, but numerical methods can be used to find an approximate solution. In this research, an application of the Finite Element Method (FEM) in Wolfram Mathematica is presented and applied to Quantum Billiards with a variety of geometries. To assess the accuracy of the method, the computed energy states are analyzed in the limit of a polygon with an increasing number of sides, the numerical results are validated against analytical solutions for geometries with known exact forms, and a standard convergence test is conducted. The FEM results closely match analytical solutions for known potentials, demonstrating its high accuracy. For high energy index n, quantum scarring may emerge for certain geometries. The nature of quantum scarring and its presence in the computed models is also investigated qualitatively.

AI.tldr: FEM in Mathematica applied to quantum billiards with various geometries, validated against analytical solutions, showing high accuracy and investigation of quantum scarring at high energy states.
AI.motivation: Closed-form solutions for quantum confinement energy spectra are only known for simple shapes (box, circle, triangle), but numerical methods are needed for more complex geometries. The research aims to demonstrate the application of FEM to quantum billiards and validate its accuracy.
AI.method: Finite Element Method (FEM) implemented in Wolfram Mathematica applied to quantum billiards with various geometries. Validation includes: 1) analyzing polygon limit with increasing sides, 2) comparing with analytical solutions for known geometries, 3) conducting standard convergence tests.
AI.result: FEM results closely match analytical solutions for known potentials, demonstrating high accuracy. For high energy index n, quantum scarring emerges in certain geometries, and its nature is investigated qualitatively.
AI.conclusion: FEM is an effective numerical method for solving quantum confinement problems in complex geometries, validated against analytical solutions. The method also enables investigation of quantum scarring phenomena in high-energy states.

title: Quantum Spectral Authentication under Public Unitary Challenges
summary: We introduce Quantum Spectral Authentication (QSA), a primitive for verifying that a remote quantum endpoint still possesses a previously installed secret quantum resource, such as a hidden state or state-preparation capability, without revealing that secret. QSA uses fresh public unitary challenges and spectral features of the planted state to derive transcript-bound session material for explicit authentication. We analyse attack strategies including eigenstate propagation across challenges, repeated-session leakage, and direct online forgery. For practical implementation, we develop a symmetric verifier-driven unitary compiler compatible with low-depth quantum phase estimation. Simulations indicate that this symmetric fast-power construction is substantially more noise tolerant than an asymmetric alternative, and small-instance experiments on IBM ibm_fez provide a hardware sanity check. QSA therefore offers a plausible near-term authentication layer for quantum networks and control-plane applications.

AI.tldr: Quantum Spectral Authentication (QSA) enables remote verification of secret quantum resources without revealing them, using public unitary challenges and spectral analysis for session-bound authentication.
AI.motivation: To provide authentication for quantum networks and control-plane applications in the near-term, enabling verification that remote quantum endpoints still possess previously installed secret quantum resources (like hidden states or state-preparation capabilities) without exposing those secrets.
AI.method: Uses fresh public unitary challenges and spectral features of the planted state to derive transcript-bound session material for explicit authentication. Includes a symmetric verifier-driven unitary compiler compatible with low-depth quantum phase estimation, with a symmetric fast-power construction that's more noise-tolerant than asymmetric alternatives.
AI.result: Simulations show the symmetric fast-power construction is substantially more noise tolerant than asymmetric alternatives. Small-instance experiments on IBM ibm_fez hardware provide a sanity check. QSA offers a plausible near-term authentication layer for quantum networks and control-plane applications.
AI.conclusion: QSA provides a practical authentication primitive for quantum systems that can verify secret quantum resources without revealing them, with demonstrated noise tolerance and hardware feasibility, making it suitable for near-term quantum network applications.

title: Adaptive Resource and Memory Control for Stability in Quantum Entanglement Distribution
summary: We investigate congestion-aware control of quantum repeater nodes operating under stochastic traffic and finite memory coherence. Entanglement generation is modeled as a probabilistic process producing Werner states subject to depolarizing memory decoherence, while entanglement requests arrive according to Poisson and bursty ON--OFF processes. Using a queueing-theoretic framework, we couple physical-layer memory dynamics with congestion-dependent service behavior to analyze stability, delay, and fidelity trade-offs. Operating regimes are characterized in terms of the load parameter, showing that fixed cutoff policies impose a fundamental fidelity--latency trade-off together with strict stability limits. Queue-aware adaptive control strategies are then introduced that dynamically adjust memory cutoff times and the number of parallel entanglement-generation channels. Cutoff adaptation restores stability near critical load by trading fidelity for service capacity, whereas resource scaling increases capacity without degrading entanglement quality. Under bursty traffic, joint adaptation suppresses delay spikes while activating additional channels only during congestion periods. The framework is further extended to a two-user shared-resource scenario in which independent traffic flows compete for a common resource pool. Stability is determined by aggregate load, while adaptive resource redistribution stabilizes queues that diverge under fixed partitioning. These results provide a queue-aware congestion-control perspective for adaptive resource management in quantum networks.

AI.tldr: The paper develops queue-aware congestion control strategies for quantum repeater networks, analyzing stability, delay, and fidelity trade-offs under stochastic traffic and memory decoherence, with adaptive policies that dynamically adjust memory cutoff times and resource allocation.
AI.motivation: Quantum networks face challenges from stochastic traffic patterns and finite memory coherence, creating congestion and fidelity degradation issues that require adaptive control strategies beyond fixed resource allocation approaches.
AI.method: A queueing-theoretic framework coupling physical-layer memory dynamics with congestion-dependent service behavior, analyzing entanglement generation as probabilistic Werner states subject to depolarizing decoherence, with traffic modeled as Poisson and bursty ON-OFF processes.
AI.result: Fixed cutoff policies impose fundamental fidelity-latency trade-offs with strict stability limits; adaptive cutoff policies restore stability near critical load by trading fidelity for capacity; resource scaling increases capacity without degrading quality; joint adaptation suppresses delay spikes under bursty traffic; adaptive resource redistribution stabilizes queues in shared-resource scenarios.
AI.conclusion: Queue-aware adaptive control strategies provide effective congestion management for quantum networks, enabling stability restoration, delay suppression, and efficient resource utilization while navigating fidelity-latency trade-offs, offering a comprehensive framework for adaptive resource management in quantum networks.

title: The Pareto Frontiers of Magic and Entanglement: The Case of Two Qubits
summary: Magic and entanglement are two measures that are widely used to characterize quantum resources. We study the interplay between magic and entanglement in two-qubit systems, focusing on the two extremes: maximal magic and minimal magic for a given level of entanglement. We quantify magic by the Rényi entropy of order 2, $M_2$, and entanglement by the concurrence $Δ$. We find that the Pareto frontier of maximal magic $M_2^{(max)}(Δ)$ is composed of three separate segments, while the boundary of minimal magic $M_2^{(min)}(Δ)$ is a single continuous line. We derive simple analytical formulas for all these four cases, and explicitly parametrize all distinct quantum states of maximal or minimal magic at a given level of entanglement.

AI.tldr: Analysis of magic-entanglement trade-off in two-qubit systems, identifying Pareto frontiers for maximal and minimal magic at given entanglement levels.
AI.motivation: To understand the interplay between two important quantum resource measures (magic and entanglement) in two-qubit systems, specifically investigating the extremes of maximal and minimal magic for fixed entanglement levels.
AI.method: Quantify magic using Rényi entropy of order 2 (M₂) and entanglement using concurrence (Δ). Analyze Pareto frontiers for maximal magic M₂^(max)(Δ) and minimal magic M₂^(min)(Δ) in two-qubit systems.
AI.result: Found that maximal magic Pareto frontier consists of three separate segments, while minimal magic boundary is a single continuous line. Derived analytical formulas for all four cases and explicitly parametrized quantum states achieving these extremes.
AI.conclusion: The study reveals structured relationships between magic and entanglement in two-qubit systems, with distinct Pareto frontiers that can be analytically characterized, providing insights into quantum resource trade-offs.

title: Test of the essential collapse-locality loophole
comment: Main text with 5 pages, 3 figures, 1 table; Supplementary Information with 5 pages and 4 figures
summary: Collapse-locality is an untested loophole in the violation of Bell's inequalities. The core of the argument is that the time value of photon detection is delayed by the time Tc required by the collapse of its quantum state. The value of Tc is given by the underlying theory of quantum collapse, and is mostly unknown. Depending on the value of Tc, detections in the performed Bell's experiments may have not been truly space-like separated events. This implies that the inequalities may have been violated as a consequence of (conspiratorial) information propagating at subluminal speed. We report an optical Bell experiment which closes the weaker ('essential') form of this loophole regardless the theory of quantum collapse. This is possible thanks to unique features of the setup. These features are: classical signals sent to the stations to define a time reference, and variable distance between the stations leaving all other parameters constant.

AI.tldr: Optical Bell experiment closes the collapse-locality loophole by ensuring truly space-like separated detections regardless of quantum collapse theory, using classical time references and variable station distances.
AI.motivation: Address the collapse-locality loophole in Bell inequality violations, where photon detection timing delays due to quantum state collapse could allow subluminal information propagation, potentially invalidating claims of nonlocality.
AI.method: Optical Bell experiment with two key features: (1) classical signals sent to stations to establish precise time reference, (2) variable distance between stations while keeping all other experimental parameters constant, enabling verification of space-like separation regardless of unknown collapse time Tc.
AI.result: Successfully closes the weaker 'essential' form of the collapse-locality loophole, demonstrating that Bell inequality violations cannot be explained by subluminal information propagation through collapse timing effects.
AI.conclusion: The experiment provides robust evidence against collapse-locality explanations of Bell violations, strengthening the case for genuine quantum nonlocality by eliminating a previously untested loophole.

title: Measurement-induced non-commutativity in adaptive fermionic linear optics
summary: Fermionic linear optics (FLO) with Gaussian resources is efficiently classically simulable. We show that this is no longer the case for such quantum circuits for fermions with internal degrees of freedom, equipped with mid-circuit number monitoring and classical feedforward. In our architecture, the measurement record routes the selected blocks into a fixed-order Bell-fusion pairing geometry. On the level of classical description, this implies realizing a situation in which the permutation sum no longer collapses to a single determinant or Pfaffian. Each post-selected branch expands as a signed sum of path-ordered products of typically non-commuting dressed blocks, and branch amplitudes are matrix elements of the resulting non-commutative trace polynomials. Numerically, we observe Porter-Thomas statistics as the output distribution and a rapid growth of the minimal order-respecting matrix product operator bond dimension. These results thus establish mid-circuit measurement-induced non-commutativity as a route to sampling hardness for noninteracting fermions under reasonable complexity assumptions, without introducing coherent two-body interactions into the FLO evolution.

AI.tldr: Fermionic linear optics with Gaussian resources is classically simulable, but adding mid-circuit measurements and classical feedforward to fermions with internal degrees of freedom makes it sampling-hard without introducing two-body interactions.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that fermionic linear optics (FLO) with Gaussian resources, which is efficiently classically simulable, can become computationally hard when enhanced with mid-circuit measurements and classical feedforward, without requiring coherent two-body interactions.
AI.method: Use fermions with internal degrees of freedom, equip FLO circuits with mid-circuit number monitoring and classical feedforward, route measurement records to create fixed-order Bell-fusion pairing geometry, and analyze the resulting non-commutative trace polynomials.
AI.result: The classical description no longer collapses to a single determinant/Pfaffian; each post-selected branch expands as signed sum of path-ordered products of non-commuting dressed blocks. Numerical evidence shows Porter-Thomas statistics in output distribution and rapid growth of minimal order-respecting matrix product operator bond dimension.
AI.conclusion: Mid-circuit measurement-induced non-commutativity provides a route to sampling hardness for noninteracting fermions under reasonable complexity assumptions, without introducing coherent two-body interactions into FLO evolution.

title: Explicit States with Two-sided Long-Range Magic
summary: Nonstabilizerness, or magic, is a necessary resource for quantum advantage beyond the classically simulatable Clifford framework. Recent works have begun to chart the structure of magic in many-body states, introducing the concepts of long-range magic -- nonstabilizerness that cannot be removed by finite-depth local unitary (FDU) circuits -- and the magic hierarchy, which classifies quantum circuits by alternating layers of Clifford and FDUs. In this work, we construct explicit states that provably possess two-sided long-range magic, a stronger form of magic meaning that they cannot be prepared by a Clifford circuit and a FDU in either order, thus placing them provably outside the first level of the magic hierarchy. Our examples include the ``magical cat" state, $|ψ\rangle \propto |0^n\rangle + |+^n\rangle$, and ground states of certain nonabelian topological orders. These results provide new examples and proof techniques for circuit complexity, and in doing so, reveal the connection between long-range magic, the structure of many-body phases, and the principles of quantum error correction.

AI.tldr: The paper constructs explicit quantum states with two-sided long-range magic that cannot be prepared by Clifford circuits followed by finite-depth unitaries in either order, placing them outside the first level of the magic hierarchy.
AI.motivation: To understand the structure of magic (nonstabilizerness) in many-body quantum systems and provide explicit examples of states with strong forms of magic that go beyond existing classifications in the magic hierarchy.
AI.method: Construct explicit quantum states including the "magical cat" state (|ψ⟩ ∝ |0ⁿ⟩ + |+ⁿ⟩) and ground states of certain nonabelian topological orders, then prove these states possess two-sided long-range magic using rigorous proof techniques.
AI.result: Demonstrates that the constructed states provably possess two-sided long-range magic, meaning they cannot be prepared by Clifford circuits followed by finite-depth local unitary circuits in either order, placing them outside the first level of the magic hierarchy.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes connections between long-range magic, many-body phase structure, and quantum error correction principles, providing new examples and proof techniques for understanding circuit complexity in quantum systems.

title: Uncertainty Quantification for Quantum Computing
summary: This review is designed to introduce mathematicians and computational scientists to quantum computing (QC) through the lens of uncertainty quantification (UQ) by presenting a mathematically rigorous and accessible narrative for understanding how noise and intrinsic randomness shape quantum computational outcomes in the language of mathematics. By grounding quantum computation in statistical inference, we highlight how mathematical tools such as probabilistic modeling, stochastic analysis, Bayesian inference, and sensitivity analysis, can directly address error propagation and reliability challenges in today's quantum devices. We also connect these methods to key scientific priorities in the field, including scalable uncertainty-aware algorithms and characterization of correlated errors. The purpose is to narrow the conceptual divide between applied mathematics, scientific computing and quantum information sciences, demonstrating how mathematically rooted UQ methodologies can guide validation, error mitigation, and principled algorithm design for emerging quantum technologies, in order to address challenges and opportunities present in modern-day quantum high performance and fault-tolerant quantum computing paradigms.

AI.tldr: A review introducing mathematicians and computational scientists to quantum computing through uncertainty quantification, showing how mathematical tools can address noise and reliability challenges in quantum devices.
AI.motivation: To bridge the conceptual gap between applied mathematics/scientific computing and quantum information sciences by demonstrating how mathematically rigorous uncertainty quantification methods can address fundamental challenges in quantum computing related to noise, error propagation, and reliability.
AI.method: The paper presents a review approach that grounds quantum computation in statistical inference, utilizing mathematical tools including probabilistic modeling, stochastic analysis, Bayesian inference, and sensitivity analysis to understand and address quantum computational uncertainties.
AI.result: The review establishes connections between uncertainty quantification methodologies and key scientific priorities in quantum computing, including scalable uncertainty-aware algorithms and characterization of correlated errors, providing a framework for validation, error mitigation, and principled algorithm design.
AI.conclusion: Mathematically rooted uncertainty quantification methodologies can effectively guide the development of emerging quantum technologies by addressing noise and reliability challenges, ultimately supporting the advancement of both near-term quantum high-performance computing and future fault-tolerant quantum computing paradigms.

title: Neural Operator Quantum State: A Foundation Model for Quantum Dynamics
summary: Capturing the dynamics of quantum many-body systems under time-dependent driving protocols is a central challenge for numerical simulations. Existing methods such as tensor networks and time-dependent neural quantum states, however, must be re-run for every protocol. In this work, we introduce the Neural Operator Quantum State (NOQS) as a foundation model for quantum dynamics. Rather than solving the Schrödinger equation for individual trajectories, our approach aims to \emph{learn the solution operator} that maps entire driving protocols to time-evolved quantum states. Once trained, the NOQS predicts time evolution under unseen protocols in a single forward pass, requiring no additional optimization. We validate NOQS on the two-dimensional Ising model with time-dependent longitudinal and transverse fields, demonstrating accurate prediction not only for unseen in-distribution protocols, but also for qualitatively different, out-of-distribution functional forms of driving. Further, a single NOQS model can be transferred between different temporal resolutions, and can be efficiently fine-tuned with sparse experimental measurements to improve predictions across all observables at negligible cost. Our work introduces a new paradigm for quantum dynamics simulation and provides a practical computational-experimental interface for driven quantum systems.

AI.tldr: NOQS is a foundation model for quantum dynamics that learns the solution operator mapping driving protocols to time-evolved quantum states, enabling single-forward-pass predictions for unseen protocols without re-optimization.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum dynamics simulation methods (tensor networks, time-dependent neural quantum states) require re-running for every driving protocol, making them inefficient for exploring multiple protocols or experimental scenarios.
AI.method: Neural Operator Quantum State (NOQS) learns the solution operator that maps entire driving protocols to time-evolved quantum states, trained on protocol-state pairs, enabling predictions for unseen protocols in a single forward pass.
AI.result: NOQS accurately predicts dynamics for 2D Ising model with time-dependent fields, works for both in-distribution and out-of-distribution driving protocols, transfers between temporal resolutions, and can be efficiently fine-tuned with sparse measurements.
AI.conclusion: NOQS introduces a new paradigm for quantum dynamics simulation as a foundation model, providing a practical computational-experimental interface for driven quantum systems with efficient protocol exploration capabilities.

title: T Count as a Numerically Solvable Minimization Problem
summary: We present a formulation of the problem of finding the smallest T -Count circuit that implements a given unitary as a binary search over a sequence of continuous minimization problems, and demonstrate that these problems are numerically solvable in practice. We reproduce best-known results for synthesis of circuits with a small number of qubits, and push the bounds of the largest circuits that can be solved for in this way. Additionally, we show that circuit partitioning can be used to adapt this technique to be used to optimize the T -Count of circuits with large numbers of qubits by breaking the circuit into a series of smaller sub-circuits that can be optimized independently.

AI.tldr: Binary search over continuous minimization problems enables T-Count optimization for quantum circuits, with circuit partitioning extending applicability to large qubit counts.
AI.motivation: The need for efficient T-Count optimization in quantum circuit synthesis, particularly for circuits with many qubits where existing methods become intractable.
AI.method: Formulate T-Count minimization as binary search over continuous optimization problems, solve numerically, and apply circuit partitioning to handle large qubit counts by breaking circuits into independently optimizable sub-circuits.
AI.result: Reproduce best-known results for small-qubit circuits, push bounds of solvable circuit sizes, and demonstrate scalability to large-qubit circuits via partitioning.
AI.conclusion: The proposed continuous optimization approach with binary search and partitioning provides a practical, scalable method for T-Count minimization in quantum circuit synthesis.

title: Hybrid photon blockade with hyperradiance in two-qubit cavity QED system
summary: We investigate a hybrid photon blockade (HPB) scheme in a driven two-qubit cavity QED system arising from the combination of eigenenergy-level anharmonicity (ELA) and quantum destructive interference (QDI). By tuning the detuning of a single qubit and pumping field, we identify precise parametric regimes that fully integrate the advantages of high brightness in ELA-based conventional photon blockade and strong antibunching in QDI-based unconventional photon blockade. Interestingly, these regimes are accompanied by hyperradiance, indicating that inter-emitter correlations give rise to enhanced collective emission. The HPB mechanism exhibits parametric generality across varying coupling asymmetries and remains accessible via detuning control, offering a feasible route for generating high-quality single-photon source in diverse quantum platforms.

AI.tldr: Hybrid photon blockade combining eigenenergy-level anharmonicity and quantum destructive interference in a two-qubit cavity QED system achieves high brightness and strong antibunching simultaneously, with hyperradiance from inter-emitter correlations.
AI.motivation: To develop a photon blockade scheme that integrates the advantages of both conventional (ELA-based) and unconventional (QDI-based) photon blockade approaches - specifically combining high brightness from ELA with strong antibunching from QDI.
AI.method: Investigates a driven two-qubit cavity QED system where HPB arises from the combination of eigenenergy-level anharmonicity and quantum destructive interference. Tunes the detuning of a single qubit and pumping field to identify precise parametric regimes that fully integrate both advantages.
AI.result: Identifies parametric regimes that achieve simultaneous high brightness and strong antibunching. These regimes are accompanied by hyperradiance, indicating enhanced collective emission from inter-emitter correlations. The HPB mechanism exhibits parametric generality across varying coupling asymmetries and remains accessible via detuning control.
AI.conclusion: The hybrid photon blockade scheme offers a feasible route for generating high-quality single-photon sources in diverse quantum platforms by combining the best features of both conventional and unconventional photon blockade approaches while leveraging inter-emitter correlations for enhanced performance.

title: Optimal measurement-based quantum thermal machines in a finite-size system
summary: We present a measurement-based quantum thermal machine that extracts work from the back-action of generalized quantum measurements whose working medium is a coupled two-level quantum system. Specifically, we derive universal optimization criteria for a three-stroke measurement-based engine cycle with coupled two-level system of Ising-like interaction as a working medium. Furthermore, we present two numerical algorithms to optimize the engine work extraction and enhance its performance. Our numerical results demonstrate: (i) efficiency peaks in the projective-measurement limit; (ii) symmetry breaking (detuning or weak coupling) enlarges the exploitable energy gap; and (iii) performance remains robust ($>50\%$ of optimum) under $\sim\!10^\circ$ feedback-pulse errors. The framework is platform-agnostic and directly implementable with current superconducting, trapped-ion, or NMR technologies, providing a concrete route to scalable, measurement-powered quantum thermal machines.

AI.tldr: Measurement-based quantum thermal machine using coupled two-level system as working medium, with optimization criteria and algorithms for work extraction, showing efficiency peaks in projective limit and robustness to errors.
AI.motivation: To develop a practical, scalable quantum thermal machine that extracts work from measurement back-action, leveraging current quantum technologies (superconducting, trapped-ion, NMR) for implementation.
AI.method: Three-stroke measurement-based engine cycle with coupled two-level system (Ising-like interaction) as working medium; derivation of universal optimization criteria; development of two numerical algorithms for optimizing work extraction.
AI.result: Efficiency peaks in projective-measurement limit; symmetry breaking (detuning/weak coupling) enlarges exploitable energy gap; performance remains robust (>50% of optimum) under ~10° feedback-pulse errors; framework is platform-agnostic and implementable with current technologies.
AI.conclusion: The measurement-based quantum thermal machine provides a concrete, scalable route to measurement-powered quantum engines that can be implemented with existing quantum technologies, demonstrating practical feasibility and robustness.

title: Reinforcement learning for quantum processes with memory
summary: In reinforcement learning, an agent interacts sequentially with an environment to maximize a reward, receiving only partial, probabilistic feedback. This creates a fundamental exploration-exploitation trade-off: the agent must explore to learn the hidden dynamics while exploiting this knowledge to maximize its target objective. While extensively studied classically, applying this framework to quantum systems requires dealing with hidden quantum states that evolve via unknown dynamics. We formalize this problem via a framework where the environment maintains a hidden quantum memory evolving via unknown quantum channels, and the agent intervenes sequentially using quantum instruments. For this setting, we adapt an optimistic maximum-likelihood estimation algorithm. We extend the analysis to continuous action spaces, allowing us to model general positive operator-valued measures (POVMs). By controlling the propagation of estimation errors through quantum channels and instruments, we prove that the cumulative regret of our strategy scales as $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{K})$ over $K$ episodes. Furthermore, via a reduction to the multi-armed quantum bandit problem, we establish information-theoretic lower bounds demonstrating that this sublinear scaling is strictly optimal up to polylogarithmic factors. As a physical application, we consider state-agnostic work extraction. When extracting free energy from a sequence of non-i.i.d. quantum states correlated by a hidden memory, any lack of knowledge about the source leads to thermodynamic dissipation. In our setting, the mathematical regret exactly quantifies this cumulative dissipation. Using our adaptive algorithm, the agent uses past energy outcomes to improve its extraction protocol on the fly, achieving sublinear cumulative dissipation, and, consequently, an asymptotically zero dissipation rate.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a quantum reinforcement learning framework for environments with hidden quantum memory and unknown dynamics, develops an optimistic maximum-likelihood algorithm with $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{K})$ regret, proves optimality via information-theoretic lower bounds, and applies it to achieve asymptotically zero dissipation in state-agnostic work extraction.
AI.motivation: Classical reinforcement learning's exploration-exploitation trade-off needs adaptation to quantum systems where environments maintain hidden quantum states evolving via unknown dynamics, requiring new frameworks to handle quantum memory and interventions.
AI.method: Formalizes quantum RL with hidden quantum memory evolving via unknown channels; agent intervenes sequentially using quantum instruments. Adapts optimistic maximum-likelihood estimation algorithm, extends to continuous action spaces for general POVMs, controls estimation error propagation through quantum channels/instruments.
AI.result: Proves cumulative regret scales as $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{K})$ over K episodes. Establishes information-theoretic lower bounds showing this sublinear scaling is optimal up to polylog factors. Applies to state-agnostic work extraction where regret quantifies thermodynamic dissipation, achieving asymptotically zero dissipation rate.
AI.conclusion: The framework successfully adapts RL to quantum systems with hidden memory, provides optimal regret bounds, and demonstrates practical application in quantum thermodynamics where adaptive learning enables asymptotically dissipation-free work extraction from correlated quantum states.

title: Banach and counting measures, and dynamics of singular quantum states generated by averaging of operator random walks
summary:
In this paper the random channels and their compositions in the space of quantum states are studied.
  For compositions of i.i.d. random unitary channels, the limit behaviour of probability distributions is described.
  The sufficient condition for convergence in probability is obtained.
  The generalized convergence in distribution w.r.t. weak operator topology is obtained.
  The analysis of transmission of pure and normal states to the set of singular states is done. The dynamics of quantum states is described in terms of the evolution of the values of quadratic forms of operators from the algebra that implements the representation of canonical commutation relations.

AI.tldr: Analysis of random quantum channels and their compositions, focusing on convergence properties and state transmission dynamics
AI.motivation: To study the statistical behavior of random quantum channels and their compositions, particularly understanding convergence properties and how quantum states evolve under repeated applications of random channels
AI.method: Analysis of compositions of i.i.d. random unitary channels, study of probability distributions, convergence conditions in probability and weak operator topology, examination of state transmission from pure/normal to singular states using quadratic forms from CCR algebra
AI.result: Obtained sufficient condition for convergence in probability, established generalized convergence in distribution w.r.t. weak operator topology, analyzed transmission dynamics between different state classes
AI.conclusion: The paper provides mathematical framework for understanding convergence and dynamics of quantum states under random channel compositions, with implications for quantum information processing and statistical quantum mechanics

title: Chiral quantum batteries
summary: Exploiting quantum effects for energy storage, quantum batteries (QBs) offer compelling advantages over conventional ones in terms of superior energy density, ultrafast charging, and high conversion efficiency. However, their realization is hampered by decoherence, which causes incomplete charging, rapid self-discharging, and reduced extractable work. Here, we propose a QB architecture based on a chiral magnonic platform. It comprises two yttrium iron garnet (YIG) spheres, one serving as the charger and the other as the QB, coupled to a waveguide. The unique chiral coupling between magnons and the guided electromagnetic fields breaks inversion symmetry, inducing both nonreciprocal energy flow and coherent interference between the charger and QB. Their synergy endows our QB with a 34-fold increase in energy capacity and a 55-fold boost in extractable work compared to its achiral counterpart in an experimentally accessible regime. Our scheme harnesses the decoherence from the electromagnetic fields and turns its destruction into an asset, which enables the robustness and wireless-like remote charging features of the QB. Our analysis reveals that these extraordinary capabilities stem from quantum coherence. By establishing chirality as a useful quantum resource, our work paves a viable path toward the realization of QBs.

AI.tldr: A quantum battery architecture using chiral magnonic platform achieves 34x energy capacity and 55x extractable work by exploiting quantum coherence and turning decoherence into an advantage.
AI.motivation: Quantum batteries offer superior energy density and charging speed but face decoherence problems causing incomplete charging, rapid self-discharging, and reduced extractable work.
AI.method: Chiral magnonic platform with two YIG spheres (charger and battery) coupled to a waveguide, using chiral coupling between magnons and guided electromagnetic fields to break inversion symmetry and create nonreciprocal energy flow with coherent interference.
AI.result: 34-fold increase in energy capacity and 55-fold boost in extractable work compared to achiral counterpart; achieves robustness and wireless-like remote charging by harnessing decoherence.
AI.conclusion: Chirality serves as a useful quantum resource that enables quantum battery realization by exploiting quantum coherence and turning decoherence from electromagnetic fields into an advantage.

title: The 27-qubit Counterexample to the LU-LC Conjecture is Minimal
summary: It was once conjectured that two graph states are local unitary (LU) equivalent if and only if they are local Clifford (LC) equivalent. This so-called LU-LC conjecture was disproved in 2007, as a pair of 27-qubit graph states that are LU-equivalent, but not LC-equivalent, was discovered. We prove that this counterexample to the LU-LC conjecture is minimal. In other words, for graph states on up to 26 qubits, the notions of LU-equivalence and LC-equivalence coincide. This result is obtained by studying the structure of 2-local complementation, a special case of the recently introduced r-local complementation, and a generalization of the well-known local complementation. We make use of a connection with triorthogonal codes and Reed-Muller codes.

AI.tldr: The paper proves that the minimal counterexample to the LU-LC conjecture is 27 qubits, showing LU and LC equivalence coincide for graph states up to 26 qubits.
AI.motivation: The LU-LC conjecture proposed that local unitary (LU) equivalence and local Clifford (LC) equivalence are identical for graph states. This was disproved in 2007 with a 27-qubit counterexample, but it remained unknown whether smaller counterexamples exist.
AI.method: The authors study the structure of 2-local complementation (a special case of r-local complementation) and its connection to triorthogonal codes and Reed-Muller codes. They use these mathematical tools to analyze graph state equivalences.
AI.result: The paper proves that 27 qubits is the minimal counterexample size - for graph states on up to 26 qubits, LU-equivalence and LC-equivalence coincide. No smaller counterexamples exist.
AI.conclusion: The LU-LC conjecture holds for graph states with up to 26 qubits, and the known 27-qubit counterexample is minimal. This provides a complete understanding of the relationship between LU and LC equivalence for graph states of different sizes.

title: Epitaxial CeO2 Films as a Host for Quantum Applications
summary: In highly purified host, the coherence of quantum emitters is ultimately limited by hyperfine interactions between the emitter and lattice nuclei possessing non-zero nuclear magnetic moments. This limitation can only be mitigated through isotopic purification. In this work, we investigate CeO2 as a host composed entirely of nuclei with zero nuclear moment. High-quality CeO2 thin films were grown by PLD and doped with Tm and Er ions. Structural characterization using X-ray diffraction, atomic force microscopy, and ion channeling confirms single-crystalline, atomically smooth films with dopants substitutionally incorporated at Ce lattice sites. Photoluminescence lifetime measurements show significantly longer lifetimes for Er-doped CeO2 (2.9 - 5.3 ms) compared with Tm-doped films (14 - 68 μs). Moreover, the Er-doped PLD films exhibit longer lifetimes at ~1% dopant concentration than previously reported for MBE-grown films. Density functional theory calculations reveal a substantial overlap between unoccupied O 2p and Tm 4f states near the valence band maximum, whereas Er 4f states remain well isolated. This electronic interaction likely introduces non-radiative recombination pathways in Tm-doped CeO2, explaining the reduced lifetimes. These findings highlight the importance of selecting appropriate dopant-host combinations and optimized growth conditions to minimize non-radiative channels for quantum applications.

AI.tldr: CeO2 as a zero-nuclear-moment host for quantum emitters shows longer Er lifetimes than Tm due to electronic interactions enabling non-radiative recombination in Tm-doped films.
AI.motivation: To overcome hyperfine interaction limitations in quantum emitters by using CeO2, a host composed entirely of nuclei with zero nuclear moment, enabling longer coherence times through isotopic purification alternatives.
AI.method: Grew high-quality CeO2 thin films by PLD doped with Tm and Er ions; performed structural characterization (XRD, AFM, ion channeling); measured photoluminescence lifetimes; conducted DFT calculations to analyze electronic structure.
AI.result: Er-doped CeO2 showed significantly longer lifetimes (2.9-5.3 ms) than Tm-doped films (14-68 μs); PLD-grown films outperformed MBE-grown ones; DFT revealed unoccupied O 2p and Tm 4f state overlap near valence band maximum, unlike isolated Er 4f states.
AI.conclusion: Selection of appropriate dopant-host combinations and optimized growth conditions is crucial to minimize non-radiative channels for quantum applications; CeO2 with Er doping shows promise as a zero-nuclear-moment host for quantum emitters.

title: Superconducting Parallel-Plate Resonators for the Detection of Single Electron Spins
comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, plus supplementary material of 5 pages, 4 figures
summary: We introduce a multilayer superconducting microwave resonator with sub-Ohm impedance optimized for high coupling strength to single electron spins. The design minimizes the magnetic far-field and therefore achieves a Purcell factor $F_P > 10^{15}$. We show several ways to fabricate this type of resonator and present resonators with an intrinsic $Q$-factor exceeding $2 \cdot 10^4$ at the single-photon level. We further characterize these resonators in magnetic fields up to $500 \, \text{mT}$. Finally, we evaluate the impact of the achievable Purcell factor on single-spin detection through photon counting and dispersive readout.

AI.tldr: Multilayer superconducting microwave resonator with sub-Ohm impedance achieves Purcell factor >10¹⁵ for strong coupling to single electron spins, with Q-factor >2×10⁴ and operation in magnetic fields up to 500 mT.
