AI.motivation: To develop a superconducting microwave resonator optimized for high coupling strength to single electron spins, enabling enhanced spin-photon interactions for quantum information processing and sensing applications.
AI.method: Multilayer superconducting resonator design with sub-Ohm impedance that minimizes magnetic far-field. Several fabrication approaches are developed and characterized. Resonators are tested at single-photon level and in magnetic fields up to 500 mT.
AI.result: Achieved Purcell factor FP > 10¹⁵, intrinsic Q-factor exceeding 2×10⁴ at single-photon level, and successful operation in magnetic fields up to 500 mT. Demonstrated impact on single-spin detection through photon counting and dispersive readout.
AI.conclusion: The multilayer superconducting microwave resonator design enables unprecedented Purcell enhancement for single electron spins, providing a promising platform for strong spin-photon coupling and enhanced spin detection techniques in quantum applications.

title: High-Fidelity Quantum State Transfer in Multimode Resonators via Tunable Pulses
summary: Quantum state transfer between distant nodes is essential for distributed quantum information processing. Existing protocols are typically optimized for specific coupling regimes, such as adiabatic dark-state transfer in the single-mode limit and pitch-and-catch schemes in the multimode regime, leaving the crossover between them without a simple and unified control strategy. Here we identify a minimal two-parameter control framework that enables high-fidelity quantum state transfer across this single-mode-to-multimode crossover in a multimode quantum channel. Using a pulse-shaped pitch-and-catch protocol controlled only by the pulse ramp rate and the emission-absorption delay, we achieve transfer fidelities exceeding 99.9%, extending pitch-and-catch protocols toward the single-mode limit without requiring dark-state protection or complex pulse design. We further demonstrate robustness against dissipation, disorder, detuning, and imperfect initialization under experimentally realistic conditions. These results provide a simple and broadly applicable framework for state transfer in multimode quantum channels, with relevance to circuit-QED and hybrid quantum-acoustic systems.

AI.tldr: A two-parameter control framework enables high-fidelity quantum state transfer across single-mode-to-multimode crossover in multimode quantum channels using pulse-shaped pitch-and-catch protocols.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum state transfer protocols are optimized for specific coupling regimes (single-mode vs. multimode), leaving the crossover between them without a simple unified control strategy.
AI.method: Developed a minimal two-parameter control framework using pulse-shaped pitch-and-catch protocol controlled only by pulse ramp rate and emission-absorption delay, without requiring dark-state protection or complex pulse design.
AI.result: Achieved transfer fidelities exceeding 99.9%, extending pitch-and-catch protocols toward the single-mode limit, with demonstrated robustness against dissipation, disorder, detuning, and imperfect initialization under realistic experimental conditions.
AI.conclusion: Provides a simple and broadly applicable framework for state transfer in multimode quantum channels with relevance to circuit-QED and hybrid quantum-acoustic systems.

title: Causality is rare: some topological properties of causal quantum channels
summary: Sorkin's impossible operations demonstrate that causality of a quantum channel in QFT is an additional constraint on quantum operations above and beyond the locality of the channel. What has not been shown in the literature so far is how much of a constraint it is. Here we answer this question in perhaps the strongest possible terms: the set of causal channels is nowhere dense in the set of local channels. We connect this result to quantum information, showing that the set of causal unitaries has Haar measure $0$ in the set of all unitaries acting on a lattice. Finally, we close with discussion on the implications and connections to recent QFT measurement models.

AI.tldr: Causal quantum channels in QFT are extremely constrained - they form a nowhere dense subset of local channels, and causal unitaries have Haar measure zero among all lattice unitaries.
AI.motivation: Sorkin's impossible operations show causality imposes constraints beyond locality in QFT, but the extent of this constraint hasn't been quantified. The paper aims to determine how restrictive causality is relative to locality.
AI.method: Mathematical analysis showing the set of causal channels is nowhere dense in the set of local channels, and connecting this to quantum information theory by demonstrating causal unitaries have Haar measure zero in the set of all unitaries on a lattice.
AI.result: Causality is an extremely strong constraint: causal channels form a nowhere dense subset of local channels, and causal unitaries have measure zero among all unitaries on a lattice, indicating causality is an exceptional property rather than generic.
AI.conclusion: Causality imposes severe restrictions on quantum operations in QFT, making causal channels exceptionally rare among local ones. This has implications for QFT measurement models and suggests causality is a highly non-generic property in quantum field theory.

title: The quantum mechanics of experiments
comment: 17 pages, submitted for publication in a special volume dedicated to Israel Michael Sigal
summary: This note starts with a recapitulation of what people call the ``Measurement Problem'' of Quantum Mechanics (QM). The dissipative nature of the quantum-mechanical time-evolution of averages of states over large ensembles of identical isolated systems consisting of matter interacting with the radiation field is discussed and shown to correspond to a stochastic time-evolution of states of individual systems. The importance of dissipation for the successful completion of measurements is highlighted. To conclude, a solution of the ``Measurement Problem'' is sketched in an idealized model of a double-slit experiment.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses the Quantum Measurement Problem by analyzing dissipative quantum evolution in large ensembles, showing it corresponds to stochastic evolution of individual systems, and proposes a solution in a double-slit experiment model.
AI.motivation: To address the long-standing "Measurement Problem" in Quantum Mechanics by examining how dissipation in quantum-mechanical time-evolution of ensemble averages relates to stochastic evolution of individual systems, and to demonstrate the role of dissipation in completing measurements.
AI.method: Recapitulates the Measurement Problem, analyzes dissipative nature of quantum-mechanical time-evolution for averages over large ensembles of isolated matter-radiation systems, shows this corresponds to stochastic evolution of individual systems, and applies this to an idealized double-slit experiment model.
AI.result: Demonstrates that dissipation in quantum evolution of ensemble averages corresponds to stochastic time-evolution of individual system states, highlighting dissipation's crucial role in measurement completion, and sketches a solution to the Measurement Problem in a double-slit experiment framework.
AI.conclusion: The Measurement Problem can be addressed by recognizing that dissipative quantum evolution of ensemble averages corresponds to stochastic evolution of individual systems, with dissipation playing an essential role in measurement processes, as illustrated in an idealized double-slit experiment model.

title: Engineering energy-time entanglement from resonance fluorescence
comment: 35 pages, 5 figures; incl. Supplementary Information (SI) with 7 SI figures, 1 SI tables;
summary: Resonance fluorescence from a coherently driven two-level emitter is a minimal quantum optical field that combines phase coherence with single-photon-level nonlinearity. Here we show that it can be engineered, using only passive linear interferometry, into energy-time entanglement. By injecting resonance fluorescence from a single quantum dot into an asymmetric Mach--Zehnder interferometer operated near destructive interference of the single-photon component, we generate an output field whose coincidence statistics are dominated by the simultaneous two-photon contribution |2> and the temporally separated photon-pair contribution |11>. In a Franson geometry, these two sectors are resolved on the coincidence-delay axis, and both exhibit high-visibility nonlocal interference fringes and violate the Clauser--Horne--Shimony--Holt Bell inequality. Our results reveal a general route for engineering entanglement from resonance fluorescence using passive optics.

AI.tldr: Resonance fluorescence from a two-level emitter can be engineered into energy-time entanglement using passive linear interferometry, specifically an asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer, generating fields with both simultaneous two-photon and temporally separated photon-pair contributions that violate Bell inequalities.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that resonance fluorescence from a coherently driven two-level emitter, which combines phase coherence with single-photon nonlinearity, can be engineered into energy-time entanglement using only passive linear interferometry, providing a general route for entanglement generation from resonance fluorescence.
AI.method: Inject resonance fluorescence from a single quantum dot into an asymmetric Mach-Zehnder interferometer operated near destructive interference of the single-photon component, generating output fields whose coincidence statistics are dominated by simultaneous two-photon contributions (|2⟩) and temporally separated photon-pair contributions (|11⟩). These sectors are resolved in a Franson geometry on the coincidence-delay axis.
AI.result: Both the |2⟩ and |11⟩ sectors exhibit high-visibility nonlocal interference fringes and violate the Clauser-Horne-Shimony-Holt (CHSH) Bell inequality, demonstrating successful generation of energy-time entanglement from resonance fluorescence using passive optics.
AI.conclusion: The results reveal a general route for engineering entanglement from resonance fluorescence using passive linear interferometry, showing that minimal quantum optical fields from two-level emitters can be transformed into useful entangled states without active components.

title: Can every set of incompatible measurements lead to genuine multipartite steering?
summary: Measurement incompatibility and bipartite quantum steering are known to display a strong connection: a set of measurements is incompatible if and only if it can lead to bipartite steering. Despite such a close link between these concepts in bipartite scenarios, little is known in the multipartite setting, where notions of genuine multipartite correlations play major roles. In this work we prove that, as in the bipartite case, incompatibility is also necessary and sufficient for genuine multipartite steering in any multipartite scenario with a single uncharacterised party. Interestingly, genuine multipartite steering can be extracted from any set of incompatible measurements using states which are not SLOCC equivalent, such as GHZ and W states. In contrast, we prove that this result does not hold in scenarios with more than one uncharacterised party, by presenting a set of incompatible measurements that can never lead to genuine multipartite steering in these cases. In order to obtain our main results, we introduce methods tailored for multipartite correlations, paving the way to understanding the role of measurement incompatibility beyond bipartite scenarios.

AI.tldr: Incompatibility is necessary and sufficient for genuine multipartite steering with one uncharacterized party, but not with multiple uncharacterized parties.
AI.motivation: While measurement incompatibility and bipartite steering are known to be equivalent, little is known about their relationship in multipartite scenarios where genuine multipartite correlations are important.
AI.method: The authors prove theoretical results about the relationship between measurement incompatibility and genuine multipartite steering, introducing methods tailored for multipartite correlations.
AI.result: 1) Incompatibility is necessary and sufficient for genuine multipartite steering with a single uncharacterized party, using states like GHZ and W states. 2) This equivalence breaks down with more than one uncharacterized party, where incompatible measurements may never lead to genuine multipartite steering.
AI.conclusion: The work establishes fundamental connections between measurement incompatibility and genuine multipartite steering, revealing both similarities and crucial differences from bipartite scenarios, while developing new methods for analyzing multipartite correlations.

title: Weak distillation of quantum resources
summary: Importance sampling based on quasi-probability decomposition is the backbone of many widely used techniques, such as error mitigation, circuit knitting, and, more generally, virtual quantum resource distillation, as it allows one to simulate operations that are not accessible in a given setting. However, this class of protocols faces a fundamental problem -- it only allows to estimate expectation values. Here, we provide a general framework that lifts any quasi-probability-based protocol from expectation value estimation to a weak simulator, realizing sampling from the desired distribution only using a restricted class of quantum resources. Our method runs with the sampling cost proportional to the negativity of the quasi-probability, in stark contrast to the naive estimation-based approach that requires a large number of samples even in the case of small negativity. We show that our method requires significantly fewer samples in a number of relevant scenarios, such as error mitigation, entanglement distillation and magic state distillation. Our framework realizes the weak simulation of quantum resources without actually distilling the state, introducing a new notion of quantum resource distillation.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a framework that transforms quasi-probability-based protocols from expectation value estimation to weak simulation, enabling sampling from desired distributions using restricted quantum resources with sampling cost proportional to quasi-probability negativity.
AI.motivation: Quasi-probability decomposition is fundamental to techniques like error mitigation, circuit knitting, and virtual quantum resource distillation, but these protocols are limited to estimating expectation values rather than enabling sampling from distributions.
AI.method: Develops a general framework that lifts any quasi-probability-based protocol to a weak simulator using a rejection sampling approach, with sampling cost scaling with the negativity of the quasi-probability distribution rather than requiring large sample numbers.
AI.result: The method achieves significantly fewer samples compared to naive estimation-based approaches in relevant scenarios including error mitigation, entanglement distillation, and magic state distillation, with sampling cost proportional to quasi-probability negativity.
AI.conclusion: The framework enables weak simulation of quantum resources without actual state distillation, introducing a new notion of quantum resource distillation that overcomes the fundamental limitation of expectation-value-only estimation in quasi-probability-based protocols.

title: Optimizing Entanglement Distribution Protocols: Maximizing Classical Information in Quantum Networks
summary: Efficient entanglement distribution is the foundational challenge in realizing large-scale Quantum Networks. However, state-of-the-art solutions are frequently limited by restrictive operational assumptions, prohibitive computational complexities, and performance metrics that misalign with practical application needs. To overcome these barriers, this paper addresses the entanglement distribution problem by introducing four pivotal advances. First, recognizing that the primary application of quantum communication is the transmission of private information, we derive the Ensemble Capacity (EC), a novel metric that explicitly quantifies the secure classical information enabled by the entanglement distribution. Second, we propose a generalized mathematical formulation that removes legacy structural restrictions in the solution space. Our formulation supports an unconstrained, arbitrary sequencing of entanglement swapping and purification. Third, to efficiently navigate the resulting combinatorial optimization space, we introduce a novel Dynamic Programming (DP)-based hypergraph generation algorithm. Unlike prior methods, our approach avoids artificial fidelity quantization, preserving exact, continuous fidelities while proactively pruning sub-optimal trajectories. Finally, we encapsulate these algorithmic solutions into CODE, a system-level, two-tiered orchestration framework designed to enable near-real-time network responsiveness. Extensive evaluations confirm that our DP-driven architecture yields superior private classical information capacity and significant reductions in computational complexity, successfully meeting the strict sub-second latency thresholds required for dynamic QN operation.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces CODE, a system-level framework for efficient entanglement distribution in Quantum Networks, featuring a novel Ensemble Capacity metric, generalized mathematical formulation, DP-based hypergraph generation, and two-tiered orchestration to meet sub-second latency requirements.
AI.motivation: Current entanglement distribution solutions are limited by restrictive operational assumptions, prohibitive computational complexities, and performance metrics that misalign with practical application needs, particularly for secure classical information transmission which is the primary application of quantum communication.
AI.method: Four key advances: 1) Derivation of Ensemble Capacity (EC) metric quantifying secure classical information enabled by entanglement; 2) Generalized mathematical formulation removing legacy structural restrictions, supporting arbitrary sequencing of entanglement swapping and purification; 3) Dynamic Programming-based hypergraph generation algorithm preserving exact continuous fidelities while pruning sub-optimal trajectories; 4) CODE system-level two-tiered orchestration framework for near-real-time network responsiveness.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations confirm superior private classical information capacity and significant reductions in computational complexity, successfully meeting strict sub-second latency thresholds required for dynamic Quantum Network operation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed CODE framework with its DP-driven architecture overcomes existing barriers in entanglement distribution, providing efficient, practical solutions that align with real-world quantum communication applications while maintaining computational feasibility for dynamic network operation.

title: Analytical Solutions of One-Dimensional ($1\mathcal{D}$) Potentials for Spin-0 Particles via the Feshbach-Villars Formalism
summary: We present a unified analytical and numerical study of the one-dimensional Feshbach--Villars (FV) equation for spin-0 particles in the presence of several representative external potentials. Starting from the FV formulation of the Klein--Gordon equation, we derive the corresponding one-dimensional master equation and analyse its solutions for Coulomb, power-exponential, Cornell, Pöschl--Teller, and Woods--Saxon interactions. For the singular Coulomb and Cornell cases, a Loudon-type cutoff regularisation is implemented on the full line, allowing a mathematically controlled treatment of the origin and an explicit classification of the states by parity. The Coulomb problem exhibits the expected near-degenerate even--odd structure in the cutoff limit, while the Cornell potential combines short-distance Coulomb behaviour with long-distance confinement and produces a finite set of bound states for fixed parameters. The power-exponential potential with $p=1$ is reduced to a Whittaker-type equation and yields an intrinsically relativistic spectrum with no standard Schrödinger bound-state limit in the parameter regime considered. For the smooth short-range Pöschl--Teller and Woods-Saxon potentials, the FV formalism reveals, respectively, the effects of definite parity and spatial asymmetry on the spectrum, wave functions, and particle--antiparticle mixing. In all cases, we reconstruct the full FV spinor, analyse the associated charge density, and compare the relativistic behaviour with the corresponding non-relativistic expectations whenever such a limit exists. The results provide a coherent set of analytical and numerical benchmarks for relativistic scalar bound states in one dimension.

AI.tldr: Analytical and numerical study of 1D Feshbach-Villars equation for spin-0 particles with various external potentials, including Coulomb, power-exponential, Cornell, Pöschl-Teller, and Woods-Saxon interactions.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified analytical and numerical framework for studying relativistic scalar bound states in one dimension using the Feshbach-Villars formalism, addressing both singular and smooth potentials with proper regularization techniques.
AI.method: Derived 1D master equation from FV formulation of Klein-Gordon equation, applied to five representative potentials. Used Loudon-type cutoff regularization for singular Coulomb and Cornell potentials. Reduced power-exponential potential to Whittaker-type equation. Analyzed smooth potentials (Pöschl-Teller, Woods-Saxon) for parity and asymmetry effects.
AI.result: Coulomb potential shows near-degenerate even-odd structure in cutoff limit; Cornell potential yields finite bound states with short-distance Coulomb and long-distance confinement behavior; power-exponential potential produces intrinsically relativistic spectrum without Schrödinger limit; smooth potentials reveal parity and asymmetry effects on spectrum, wave functions, and particle-antiparticle mixing.
AI.conclusion: The study provides coherent analytical and numerical benchmarks for relativistic scalar bound states in 1D, demonstrating the FV formalism's utility for both singular and smooth potentials, with insights into regularization, parity classification, and relativistic vs. non-relativistic behavior comparisons.

title: A derivation of the late-time volume law for local operator entanglement
summary: Local Operator Entanglement (LOE) has emerged an indicator of quantum chaos in many-body systems. Numerical studies have shown that, in chaotic systems, LOE grows linearly in time and displays a volume-law behavior at late times, scaling proportionally with the number of local degrees of freedom. Despite extensive numerical evidence, complemented by analytical studies in integrable systems, a fully analytical understanding of the emergence of the volume law remains incomplete. In this paper, we contribute toward this goal by deriving a late-time expression for LOE in chaotic systems that exhibits volume-law scaling. Our derivation proceeds by expressing the late-time LOE in the Liouville eigenstate basis and relies on three main assumptions: a higher-order non-resonance condition for the Hamiltonian eigenenergies, the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH) ansatz for the matrix elements of the initial local operator, and the replacement of Hamiltonian eigenstates with random states in the final expression for LOE. Under these assumptions, we obtain an explicit formula displaying volume-law scaling. Finally, we complement our analytical derivation with numerical simulations of the 1D mixed-field Ising model, testing the resulting formula and exploring the regime of validity of our assumptions.

AI.tldr: Analytical derivation of volume-law scaling for Local Operator Entanglement in chaotic quantum systems using Liouville eigenstate basis, non-resonance conditions, ETH ansatz, and random state approximation.
AI.motivation: Despite numerical evidence showing Local Operator Entanglement (LOE) grows linearly and exhibits volume-law scaling in chaotic systems, a complete analytical understanding of this emergent volume law remains lacking.
AI.method: Derive late-time LOE expression in Liouville eigenstate basis using three key assumptions: higher-order non-resonance condition for Hamiltonian eigenenergies, ETH ansatz for initial local operator matrix elements, and replacement of Hamiltonian eigenstates with random states.
AI.result: Obtain explicit analytical formula for LOE displaying volume-law scaling, validated through numerical simulations of the 1D mixed-field Ising model, testing formula validity and assumption regimes.
AI.conclusion: Provides analytical foundation for volume-law scaling of LOE in chaotic quantum systems, bridging gap between numerical observations and theoretical understanding through systematic derivation and numerical verification.

title: Quantum Finite Temperature Lanczos Method
summary: The computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in our understanding of quantum mechanics. We introduce the Quantum Finite Temperature Lanczos Method (QFTLM), which extends the finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers by combining real-time quantum Krylov methods with efficient preparation of typical states for trace estimation. This approach enables the computation of thermal expectation values while avoiding the exponential scaling inherent to classical exact simulation techniques. Numerical experiments on the transverse-field Ising model show that QFTLM can reproduce thermal observables over a wide temperature range. We further analyze the influence of Krylov dimension, number of trace-estimator states, and Trotter error, and show that suitable regularization is essential for robustness in noisy settings. These results establish QFTLM as a promising framework for finite-temperature quantum simulation.

AI.tldr: QFTLM extends finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers using real-time quantum Krylov methods and typical state preparation for trace estimation, enabling thermal property computation without exponential classical scaling.
AI.motivation: Computation of thermal properties of quantum many-body systems is a central challenge in quantum mechanics, requiring methods that avoid exponential scaling inherent to classical exact simulation techniques.
AI.method: Quantum Finite Temperature Lanczos Method (QFTLM) combines real-time quantum Krylov methods with efficient preparation of typical states for trace estimation to compute thermal expectation values on quantum computers.
AI.result: Numerical experiments on transverse-field Ising model show QFTLM can reproduce thermal observables over wide temperature range; analysis reveals importance of Krylov dimension, number of trace-estimator states, Trotter error, and regularization for robustness in noisy settings.
AI.conclusion: QFTLM establishes a promising framework for finite-temperature quantum simulation by extending classical finite-temperature Lanczos method to quantum computers with demonstrated effectiveness and robustness considerations.

title: From Complementarity to Quantum Properties: An Operational Reconstructive Approach
summary: Quantum theory brings into question the compatibility of the twin desiderata of exact knowability of the present state of the physical world and perfect predictability of its future states. Bohr's coordination-causality complementarity principle transforms this tension into one between properties (as ordinarily understood in classical physics) and deterministic causality. Here, we develop an explicit model of quantum properties which accommodates this essential tension. Our approach integrates operational, reconstructive, and metaphysical standpoints. In particular, we make use of an operational framework employed in a recent operational reconstruction of Feynman's formulation of quantum theory; base our property model on an analysis of property types; and use the notions of actuality and potentiality to frame the model. We show that this quantum property model provides a natural resolution of Zeno's paradox of motion, and provides reliable intuitions about phenomena such as electron diffraction and the non-local behaviour of entangled states of non-identical particles.

AI.tldr: Quantum property model integrating operational, reconstructive, and metaphysical approaches to resolve tension between knowability and predictability, providing intuitive explanations for quantum phenomena.
AI.motivation: Address the fundamental tension in quantum theory between exact knowability of present states and perfect predictability of future states, as highlighted by Bohr's coordination-causality complementarity principle.
AI.method: Develop an explicit quantum property model integrating operational, reconstructive, and metaphysical standpoints: uses operational framework from Feynman formulation reconstruction, analyzes property types, and employs actuality-potentiality concepts.
AI.result: The quantum property model naturally resolves Zeno's paradox of motion and provides reliable intuitions for electron diffraction and non-local behavior of entangled states of non-identical particles.
AI.conclusion: The integrated approach successfully models quantum properties to accommodate the essential tension between knowability and predictability, offering intuitive understanding of key quantum phenomena.

title: A counterexample to the strong spin alignment conjecture
summary: The spin alignment conjecture was originally formulated in connection with the additivity of coherent information for a class of quantum channels known as platypus channels. Recently, a stronger majorization-based version was proposed by M. A. Alhejji and E. Knill [Commun. Math. Phys. 405, 119, 2024], asserting that the spectrum of the alignment operator is always majorized by that of the perfectly aligned configuration. In this letter, we show that this strong spin alignment conjecture is false in general by constructing an explicit counterexample in the smallest unresolved case, namely three qubits. The example uses two-body states that are not jointly compatible with any single three-qubit global state, which naturally leads to a compatibility-constrained variant of the conjecture.

AI.tldr: The strong spin alignment conjecture (majorization version) is disproven via a three-qubit counterexample using incompatible two-body states.
AI.motivation: To test the validity of the strong spin alignment conjecture proposed by Alhejji and Knill, which asserts that the spectrum of the alignment operator is always majorized by that of the perfectly aligned configuration.
AI.method: Construct an explicit counterexample in the smallest unresolved case (three qubits) using two-body states that are not jointly compatible with any single three-qubit global state.
AI.result: The strong spin alignment conjecture is false in general, as demonstrated by the constructed three-qubit counterexample.
AI.conclusion: The majorization-based version of the spin alignment conjecture does not hold universally, leading to a proposed compatibility-constrained variant of the conjecture.

title: Mass-correction-induced enhancement of quantum correlations even beyond entanglement in the $e^{+}e^{-} \rightarrow J/ψ\rightarrow Λ(pπ^{-}) \barΛ(\bar{p}π^{+})$ process at the BESIII experiment under memory effects
summary: In this work, we derive the bipartite density matrix for the $e^{+}e^{-} \rightarrow J/ψ\rightarrow Λ(pπ^{-}) \barΛ(\bar{p}π^{+})$ process at BESIII. We evaluate the impact of mass corrections and memory effects (within Markovian and non-Markovian regimes) on quantum correlations even beyond entanglement. The dependence of these quantum properties on the scattering angle $\varphi$ is analyzed, with a particular focus on the impact of mass corrections. By comparing massless and mass-corrected scenarios, we demonstrate that the inclusion of mass effects enhances the maximum violation of the Bell inequality. While the qualitative temporal behavior remains unchanged, mass corrections quantitatively modify the angular distribution and introduce additional extrema at $\varphi=0$ and $\varphi=π$, thereby strengthening non-local correlations without altering their fundamental dynamical origin. An examination of the hierarchy of quantum correlations in baryon-antibaryon systems yields partial confirmation: $\text{Bell Nonlocality} \subset \text{Steering} \subset \text{Entanglement} \subset \text{Discord}$. Additionally, our results show that classical correlations serve to mitigate the decoherence and the decay of quantum correlations. This interplay between classical and quantum correlations suggests practical applications in quantum information and provides a robust framework for investigating baryon-antibaryon interactions.

AI.tldr: Mass corrections enhance Bell inequality violation in J/ψ→ΛΛ̅ decay, modifying angular distributions while preserving qualitative dynamics, with classical correlations mitigating decoherence.
AI.motivation: To analyze quantum correlations (including entanglement, steering, Bell nonlocality, and discord) in baryon-antibaryon systems from J/ψ decay, specifically investigating the impact of mass corrections and memory effects on these quantum properties.
AI.method: Derived bipartite density matrix for e⁺e⁻→J/ψ→Λ(pπ⁻)Λ̅(p̅π⁺) process at BESIII, evaluated mass corrections and memory effects (Markovian/non-Markovian regimes), analyzed quantum correlation dependence on scattering angle φ, compared massless vs. mass-corrected scenarios.
AI.result: Mass corrections enhance maximum Bell inequality violation, modify angular distribution quantitatively (introducing extrema at φ=0 and φ=π), preserve qualitative temporal behavior, confirm hierarchy: Bell Nonlocality ⊂ Steering ⊂ Entanglement ⊂ Discord, and show classical correlations mitigate decoherence and quantum correlation decay.
AI.conclusion: Mass effects strengthen non-local correlations without altering fundamental dynamics, classical-quantum correlation interplay has practical quantum information applications, and the framework provides robust investigation of baryon-antibaryon interactions.

title: Maximizing Qubit Throughput under Buffer Decoherence and Variability in Generation
summary:
Quantum communication networks require transmission of high-fidelity, uncoded qubits for applications such as entanglement distribution and quantum key distribution. However, current implementations are constrained by limited buffer capacity and qubit decoherence, which degrades qubit quality while waiting in the buffer. A key challenge arises from the stochastic nature of qubit generation, there exists a random delay (D) between the initiation of a generation request and the availability of the qubit. This induces a fundamental trade off early initiation increases buffer waiting time and hence decoherence, whereas delayed initiation leads to server idling and reduced throughput.
  We model this system as an admission control problem in a finite buffer queue, where the reward associated with each job is a decreasing function of its sojourn time. We derive analytical conditions under which a simple "no lag" policy where a new qubit is generated immediately upon the availability of buffer space is optimal. To address scenarios with unknown system parameters, we further develop a Bayesian learning framework that adaptively optimizes the admission policy. In addition to quantum communication systems, the proposed model is applicable to delay sensitive IoT sensing and service systems.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses the trade-off between early vs. delayed qubit generation in quantum communication networks, modeling it as an admission control problem with decoherence-dependent rewards and developing optimal policies including a Bayesian learning approach for unknown parameters.
AI.motivation: Quantum communication networks need high-fidelity qubit transmission for applications like entanglement distribution and QKD, but face challenges from limited buffer capacity and qubit decoherence during waiting. The stochastic nature of qubit generation creates a fundamental trade-off: early initiation increases buffer waiting time and decoherence, while delayed initiation causes server idling and reduced throughput.
AI.method: Model the system as an admission control problem in a finite buffer queue where reward per job decreases with sojourn time. Derive analytical conditions for optimality of a "no lag" policy (immediate generation upon buffer space availability). Develop a Bayesian learning framework to adaptively optimize admission policy when system parameters are unknown.
AI.result: Established conditions under which the simple "no lag" policy is optimal. Created a Bayesian learning framework that can adaptively optimize admission policies for scenarios with unknown system parameters.
AI.conclusion: The proposed model effectively addresses the fundamental trade-off in quantum communication networks between decoherence and throughput, providing both analytical optimality conditions and adaptive learning approaches for practical implementation. The framework also has broader applicability to delay-sensitive IoT sensing and service systems.

title: Networks of quantum reference frames and the nature of conserved quantities
summary: We show that networks of quantum frames of reference, in which one frame may be used to produce multiple other frames that in their turn prepare systems which may interact with one another, have counterintuitive properties that make following the exchange of conserved quantities very subtle, and raise questions about the very nature of conserved quantities. In addition, we present an alternative approach to analysing quantum reference frames that we believe will be useful in discussions related to quantum frames of reference.

AI.tldr: Quantum reference frame networks exhibit counterintuitive properties that challenge conventional understanding of conserved quantities, requiring new analytical approaches.
AI.motivation: To investigate the subtle and counterintuitive properties of quantum reference frame networks, particularly how conserved quantities behave when one frame produces multiple other frames that prepare interacting systems, raising fundamental questions about the nature of conserved quantities in quantum mechanics.
AI.method: Analysis of networks of quantum frames of reference where frames can generate multiple other frames, which in turn prepare systems that interact with each other. The paper also presents an alternative analytical approach specifically designed for discussing quantum reference frames.
AI.result: The research reveals that quantum reference frame networks have counterintuitive properties that make tracking the exchange of conserved quantities extremely subtle. These findings challenge conventional understanding and raise fundamental questions about the nature of conserved quantities in quantum mechanics.
AI.conclusion: Quantum reference frame networks exhibit fundamentally different behavior from classical reference frames, requiring new analytical tools and approaches to properly understand the subtle exchange of conserved quantities, with implications for our understanding of conservation laws in quantum mechanics.

title: Send the Key in Cleartext: Halving Key Consumption while Preserving Unconditional Security in QKD Authentication
summary: Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) protocols require Information-Theoretically Secure (ITS) authentication of the classical channel to preserve the unconditional security of the distilled key. Standard ITS schemes are based on one-time keys: once a key is used to authenticate a message, it must be discarded. Since QKD requires mutual authentication, two independent one-time keys are typically consumed per round, imposing a non-trivial overhead on the net secure key rate. In this work, we present the authentication-with-response scheme, a novel ITS authentication scheme based on $\varepsilon$-Almost Strongly Universal$_2$ ($\varepsilon$-ASU$_2$) functions, whose IT security can be established in the Universal Composability (UC) framework. The scheme achieves mutual authentication consuming a single one-time key per QKD round, halving key consumption compared to the state-of-the-art.

AI.tldr: A novel authentication scheme for QKD that halves key consumption by using ε-ASU₂ functions to achieve mutual authentication with a single one-time key per round instead of two.
AI.motivation: QKD requires ITS authentication of classical channels to maintain unconditional security, but standard ITS schemes consume two one-time keys per round for mutual authentication, creating significant overhead that reduces net secure key rates.
AI.method: Developed an authentication-with-response scheme based on ε-ASU₂ functions, with IT security established in the Universal Composability framework, enabling mutual authentication while consuming only one one-time key per QKD round.
AI.result: The scheme reduces key consumption by 50% compared to state-of-the-art methods, achieving mutual authentication with a single one-time key per QKD round while maintaining information-theoretic security.
AI.conclusion: The authentication-with-response scheme significantly improves QKD efficiency by halving authentication key overhead while preserving unconditional security through formal UC framework analysis.

title: Nonperturbative Resummation of Divergent Time-Local Generators
summary: Time-local generators of open quantum systems are generically divergent at long times, even though the reduced dynamics remains regular. We construct, by analytic continuation, nonperturbative dynamical maps consistent with these generators. For the weak-coupling unbiased spin--boson model, this construction yields an explicit dynamical map that nonperturbatively resums the TCL generator and exposes how the divergences signal the approach to a singular time at which the reduced dynamics becomes noninvertible. The reconstructed map is validated against TEMPO simulations at short times and the exactly solvable rotating-wave model at all times. In the full spin--boson model, the same continuum mechanism produces both an early-time anisotropy, with a measurable phase shift that provides a signature of the environmental correlation and the pointer direction, and a late-time singularity at which the reduced dynamics becomes noninvertible. By contrast, in the rotating-wave model the map approaches this point without reaching it and remains invertible at all times. These results establish a nonperturbative framework for reconstructing reduced dynamics from divergent time-local generators, diagnosing the onset of noninvertibility, and identifying experimentally accessible early-time signatures of environment-induced anisotropy.

AI.tldr: Nonperturbative reconstruction of quantum dynamical maps from divergent time-local generators, revealing how divergences signal noninvertibility and early-time anisotropy signatures.
AI.motivation: Time-local generators of open quantum systems often diverge at long times despite regular reduced dynamics, creating a need to understand and reconstruct consistent dynamical maps from these divergent generators.
AI.method: Construct nonperturbative dynamical maps via analytic continuation of divergent time-local generators, specifically applying this to the weak-coupling unbiased spin-boson model and comparing with TEMPO simulations and the exactly solvable rotating-wave model.
AI.result: Successfully reconstructed explicit dynamical map that nonperturbatively resums the TCL generator, showing divergences signal approach to singular time where reduced dynamics becomes noninvertible. The map reveals early-time anisotropy with measurable phase shift and late-time singularity in full spin-boson model, while rotating-wave model approaches but never reaches this point.
AI.conclusion: Established nonperturbative framework for reconstructing reduced dynamics from divergent time-local generators, diagnosing noninvertibility onset, and identifying experimentally accessible early-time signatures of environment-induced anisotropy.

title: Kardashev scale Quantum Computing for Bitcoin Mining
summary: Bitcoin already faces a quantum threat through Shor attacks on elliptic-curve signatures. This paper isolates the other component that public discussion often conflates with it: mining. Grover's algorithm halves the exponent of brute-force search, promising a quadratic edge to any quantum miner of Bitcoin. Exactly how large that edge grows depends on fault-tolerant hardware. No prior study has costed that hardware end to end. We build an open-source estimator that sweeps the full attack surface: reversible oracles for double-SHA-256 mining and RIPEMD-based address preimages, surface-code factory sizing, fleet logistics under Nakamoto-consensus timing, and Kardashev-scale energy accounting. A parametric sweep over difficulty bits b, runtime caps, and target success probabilities reveals a sharp transition. At the most favourable partial-preimage setting (b = 32, 2^224 marked states), a superconducting surface-code fleet still requires about 10^8 physical qubits and about 10^4 MW. That load is comparable to a large national grid. Tightening to Bitcoin's January 2025 mainnet difficulty (b about 79) explodes the bill to about 10^23 qubits and about 10^25 W, approaching the Kardashev Type II threshold. These numbers settle a narrower question than "Is Bitcoin quantum-secure?" Once Grover mining is lifted from asymptotic query counts to fault-tolerant physical cost, practical quantum mining collapses under oracle, distillation, and fleet overhead. To push mining into non-trivial consensus effects, one must invoke astronomical quantum fleets operating at energy scales that lie far above present-day civilization.

AI.tldr: Quantum Bitcoin mining using Grover's algorithm requires astronomical resources - from 10^8 qubits/10^4 MW for easy settings to 10^23 qubits/10^25 W for real Bitcoin difficulty, making practical quantum mining infeasible.
AI.motivation: To quantify the actual physical costs of quantum Bitcoin mining using Grover's algorithm, moving beyond asymptotic query counts to realistic fault-tolerant hardware requirements, surface-code factory sizing, fleet logistics, and energy accounting.
AI.method: Built an open-source estimator that sweeps the full attack surface: reversible oracles for double-SHA-256 mining and RIPEMD-based address preimages, surface-code factory sizing, fleet logistics under Nakamoto-consensus timing, and Kardashev-scale energy accounting. Conducted parametric sweeps over difficulty bits b, runtime caps, and target success probabilities.
AI.result: Revealed a sharp transition in resource requirements: at favorable partial-preimage setting (b=32, 2^224 marked states), requires ~10^8 physical qubits and ~10^4 MW (comparable to large national grid). At Bitcoin's January 2025 mainnet difficulty (b≈79), requirements explode to ~10^23 qubits and ~10^25 W, approaching Kardashev Type II threshold.

To achieve non-trivial consensus effects requires astronomical quantum fleets operating at energy scales far beyond present-day civilization.

title: Adaptive Negativity Estimation via Collective Measurements
summary: This paper explores an efficient method for entanglement quantification in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit quantum systems based upon the framework of collective measurements in conjunction with machine learning. We introduce an adaptive measurement procedure in which measurement settings are dynamically adjusted based on prior measurement outcomes aiming to optimize the inference precision given a limited number of these measurement settings. The procedure makes use of the Long Short-Term Memory networks to recurrently process collective measurements on two copies of the investigated states. Obtained results demonstrate the tangible benefits of the adaptive measurements in comparison to previously described non-adaptive strategies.

AI.tldr: Adaptive collective measurements with LSTM networks improve entanglement quantification in two-qubit and qubit-qutrit systems over non-adaptive methods.
AI.motivation: To develop more efficient entanglement quantification methods that optimize measurement resources by dynamically adjusting settings based on prior outcomes, improving precision with limited measurements.
AI.method: Adaptive measurement procedure using Long Short-Term Memory networks to process collective measurements on two copies of quantum states, with settings dynamically adjusted based on prior measurement outcomes.
AI.result: Demonstrated tangible benefits of adaptive measurements over previously described non-adaptive strategies for entanglement quantification.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive collective measurements combined with machine learning provide superior entanglement quantification efficiency compared to non-adaptive approaches.

title: Stochastic Multipath Routing for High-Throughput Entanglement Distribution in Quantum Repeater Networks
comment: 11 pages, 6 figures in main text, 3 figures in SM
summary: Quantum repeater networks distribute entanglement over lossy links while many users share a limited pool of entangled pairs. Most existing routing schemes either always use a single best path or rely on global optimizations that are hard to run in real time. Here we propose and analyze a simple alternative: a stochastic multipath rule in which each entanglement request is sent at random along one of several edge-disjoint repeater paths, with a single parameter that controls the bias between shorter and longer routes. Using a distance-dependent lossy network model with finite per-link capacities and probabilistic entanglement swapping, we develop an analytic description of the resulting end-to-end entanglement rate as a function of this bias and validate it with large-scale numerical simulations. We find that an intermediate bias consistently outperforms both deterministic extremes across distances, traffic patterns, attenuation, swapping noise, and congestion, bringing the rate close to simple capacity upper bounds and making link usage more even across networks. These results identify stochastic multipath routing as a lightweight classical control strategy for boosting performance and scalability in near-term quantum repeater networks.

AI.tldr: Stochastic multipath routing for quantum repeater networks outperforms deterministic single-path approaches by balancing shorter and longer routes, improving entanglement rates and network utilization.
AI.motivation: Existing quantum repeater routing schemes either use a single best path (too rigid) or rely on complex global optimizations (impractical for real-time operation). There's a need for simple, effective routing strategies that can handle limited entangled pair resources and lossy links.
AI.method: Proposes a stochastic multipath routing rule where each entanglement request is randomly sent along one of several edge-disjoint repeater paths, controlled by a single parameter that biases selection between shorter and longer routes. Uses a distance-dependent lossy network model with finite per-link capacities and probabilistic entanglement swapping.
AI.result: Intermediate bias consistently outperforms both deterministic extremes across various conditions (distances, traffic patterns, attenuation, swapping noise, congestion). Achieves rates close to simple capacity upper bounds and makes link usage more even across networks.
AI.conclusion: Stochastic multipath routing is a lightweight classical control strategy that boosts performance and scalability in near-term quantum repeater networks, offering a practical alternative to complex optimization approaches.

title: A unified quantum computing quantum Monte Carlo framework through structured state preparation
summary: We extend Quantum Computing Quantum Monte Carlo (QCQMC) beyond ground-state energy estimation by systematically constructing the quantum circuits used for state preparation. Replacing the original Variational Quantum Eigensolver (VQE) prescription with task-adapted unitaries, we show that QCQMC can address excited-state spectra via Variational Fast Forwarding and the Variational Unitary Matrix Product Operator (VUMPO), combinatorial optimization via a symmetry-preserving VQE ansatz, and finite-temperature observables via Haar-random unitaries. Benchmarks on molecular, condensed-matter, nuclear-structure, and graph-optimization problems demostrate that the QMC diffusion step consistently improves the energy accuracy of the underlying state-preparation method across all tested domains. For weakly correlated systems, VUMPO achieves near-exact energies with significantly shallower circuits by offloading optimization to a classical tensor-network pre-training step, while for strongly correlated systems, the QMC correction becomes essential. We further provide a proof-of-concept demonstration that Haar-random basis state preparation within QCQMC yields finite-temperature estimates from pure-state dynamics.

AI.tldr: QCQMC extends beyond ground-state energy estimation by using task-adapted unitaries for state preparation, enabling applications to excited states, combinatorial optimization, and finite-temperature observables with improved accuracy across multiple domains.
AI.motivation: To extend Quantum Computing Quantum Monte Carlo (QCQMC) beyond its original ground-state energy estimation capabilities by systematically constructing quantum circuits for state preparation, enabling broader applications in quantum chemistry, condensed matter, nuclear structure, and combinatorial optimization.
AI.method: Replace original VQE prescription with task-adapted unitaries: Variational Fast Forwarding and VUMPO for excited-state spectra, symmetry-preserving VQE ansatz for combinatorial optimization, and Haar-random unitaries for finite-temperature observables. Use QMC diffusion step to improve energy accuracy of underlying state-preparation methods.
AI.result: QMC diffusion step consistently improves energy accuracy across molecular, condensed-matter, nuclear-structure, and graph-optimization problems. VUMPO achieves near-exact energies with shallower circuits for weakly correlated systems via classical tensor-network pre-training. For strongly correlated systems, QMC correction becomes essential. Haar-random basis state preparation yields finite-temperature estimates from pure-state dynamics.
AI.conclusion: QCQMC can be successfully extended beyond ground-state energy estimation through systematic construction of task-adapted quantum circuits, demonstrating broad applicability across quantum chemistry, physics, and optimization domains with consistently improved accuracy through the QMC diffusion step.

title: Robust continuous-variable multipartite entanglement in circular arrays of nonlinear waveguides
summary: Encoding continuous-variable quantum information in the optical domain has recently enabled the generation of large entangled states, yet robust implementation remains a challenge. Here, we present a straightforward protocol for generating multipartite entanglement based on spontaneous parametric down-conversion in a circular array of quadratic nonlinear waveguides. We provide a rigorous theoretical framework, including comprehensive derivations of the propagation equations and the identification of regimes where analytical solutions are possible. Crucially, our approach identifies the pump and detection configurations required to sustain and measure multipartite full inseparability across arbitrary propagation distances and for any number of waveguides $N=4 n$. This regime, elusive to standard numerical methods, represents a key requirement for scalable quantum protocols. Our scheme is inherently robust as it relies on phase-matched propagation eigenmodes, making it resilient against variations in sample length, coupling, and nonlinearity.

AI.tldr: Protocol for generating robust multipartite entanglement using spontaneous parametric down-conversion in circular arrays of quadratic nonlinear waveguides, with analytical solutions for scalable quantum protocols.
AI.motivation: While continuous-variable quantum encoding in optics enables large entangled states, robust implementation remains challenging. Current approaches lack analytical solutions for scalable multipartite entanglement generation.
AI.method: Uses spontaneous parametric down-conversion in circular arrays of quadratic nonlinear waveguides. Provides rigorous theoretical framework with propagation equations, identifies pump/detection configurations for multipartite full inseparability across arbitrary distances for N=4n waveguides. Relies on phase-matched propagation eigenmodes.
AI.result: Identifies regimes with analytical solutions (elusive to standard numerical methods) for sustaining and measuring multipartite full inseparability. Approach is inherently robust against variations in sample length, coupling, and nonlinearity.
AI.conclusion: The protocol provides a straightforward, robust method for generating scalable multipartite entanglement using circular waveguide arrays, addressing key requirements for practical quantum protocols with analytical solutions.

title: Weighted Nested Commutators for Scalable Counterdiabatic State Preparation
comment: 5-page letter (4 figures) + 7-page supplement (4 figures). Comments are welcome
summary: Counterdiabatic (CD) driving enables efficient quantum state preparation, but it requires implementing highly nonlocal adiabatic gauge potentials (AGP) that are impractical to compute and realize in large many-body systems. We introduce a \textit{weighted nested-commutator} (WNC) ansatz to approximate AGP using local operators. The WNC ansatz generalizes the standard nested-commutator ansatz by assigning independent variational weights to commutators of local Hamiltonian terms, thereby enlarging the variational space while preserving a fixed operator range. We show that the WNC ansatz can be efficiently optimized using a local optimization scheme. Moreover, it systematically outperforms the nested-commutator ansatz in preparing one-dimensional matrix product states (MPS) and the ground state of a nonintegrable quantum Ising model. We then numerically demonstrate that CD driving based on the WNC ansatz significantly accelerates the preparation of 1D MPS for system sizes up to $N = 1000$ qubits, as well as the two-dimensional Affleck-Kennedy-Lieb-Tasaki state on a hexagonal lattice with up to $N = 3 \times 10$ sites.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a weighted nested-commutator ansatz to approximate adiabatic gauge potentials for counterdiabatic driving, enabling efficient quantum state preparation in large many-body systems with local operators.
AI.motivation: Counterdiabatic driving requires implementing highly nonlocal adiabatic gauge potentials that are impractical to compute and realize in large many-body systems, creating a need for practical approximations using local operators.
AI.method: Introduces a weighted nested-commutator ansatz that generalizes the standard nested-commutator approach by assigning independent variational weights to commutators of local Hamiltonian terms, enlarging the variational space while preserving fixed operator range. Includes a local optimization scheme for efficient optimization.
AI.result: The WNC ansatz systematically outperforms the nested-commutator ansatz in preparing one-dimensional matrix product states and ground states of nonintegrable quantum Ising models. Enables significant acceleration of state preparation for 1D MPS up to 1000 qubits and 2D AKLT states on hexagonal lattices up to 3×10 sites.
AI.conclusion: The weighted nested-commutator ansatz provides an effective variational approach for approximating adiabatic gauge potentials with local operators, enabling practical counterdiabatic driving for efficient quantum state preparation in large-scale many-body systems.

title: Symplectic Split-Operator Propagators from Tridiagonalized Multi-Mode Bosonic Hilbert Spaces for Bose-Hubbard Hamiltonians
summary: In this methods paper, we show how to tridia\-go\-nalize two families of bosonic multimode systems: optomechanical and Bose-Hubbard hamiltonians. Using tools from number theory, we devise a rendering of these systems in the form of exact $D \times D$ tridiagonal symmetric matrices with real-valued entries. Such matrices can subsequently be exactly diagonalized using specialized sparse-matrix algorithms that need on the order of $D \ln(D)$ steps. This makes it possible to describe systems with much larger numbers of basis states than available to date. It also allows for efficient diagonal representation of large, accurate, symplectic split-operator propagators for which we moreover show that the required basis changes can be implemented by simple re-indexing, at marginal computational cost.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a method to tridiagonalize bosonic multimode systems (optomechanical and Bose-Hubbard) using number theory, enabling efficient diagonalization and propagation for large systems.
AI.motivation: Current methods for analyzing bosonic multimode systems are computationally limited, restricting the size of systems that can be accurately described and simulated.
AI.method: Using number theory tools to render bosonic multimode systems as exact D×D tridiagonal symmetric matrices with real entries, enabling efficient diagonalization via sparse-matrix algorithms requiring O(D ln D) steps.
AI.result: Enables description of systems with much larger numbers of basis states than previously possible, and allows efficient implementation of symplectic split-operator propagators with minimal computational overhead for basis changes.
AI.conclusion: The method provides a significant computational advantage for analyzing large bosonic multimode systems, making previously intractable problems computationally feasible through efficient tridiagonalization and diagonalization techniques.

title: Scalable Qauntum Interference from Indistinguishable Quantum Dots
summary: Quantum interference of indistinguishable photons is the foundation of photonic quantum technologies, yet scaling from a few to many identical quantum light sources remains a major challenge. In solid-state platforms, spatial and spectral inhomogeneity and resource-intensive architectures impede scaling. As a result, interference between remote, independent quantum emitters has been thus far limited to pairs. Here we introduce a wavefront-shaping approach that enables scalable interference from multiple indistinguishable quantum dots on the same chip. Using programmable spatial light modulators, we independently excite, collect, and route emission from spatially distinct, yet spectrally degenerate dots. Scaling from two to five indistinguishable emitters, we verify interference through cooperative-emission phenomena and Hong-Ou-Mandel two-photon interference, thereby establishing a route towards large-scale, programmable quantum photonic architectures.

AI.tldr: Wavefront shaping enables scalable quantum interference from multiple indistinguishable quantum dots on a single chip, overcoming previous limitations to just two emitters.
AI.motivation: Scaling quantum interference from a few to many identical quantum light sources remains a major challenge in photonic quantum technologies due to spatial/spectral inhomogeneity and resource-intensive architectures in solid-state platforms.
AI.method: Wavefront-shaping approach using programmable spatial light modulators to independently excite, collect, and route emission from spatially distinct but spectrally degenerate quantum dots on the same chip.
AI.result: Successfully scaled from two to five indistinguishable emitters, verified interference through cooperative-emission phenomena and Hong-Ou-Mandel two-photon interference.
AI.conclusion: Establishes a route towards large-scale, programmable quantum photonic architectures by overcoming previous limitations on scaling quantum interference from multiple independent quantum emitters.

title: Provably Efficient Long-Time Exponential Decompositions of Non-Markovian Gaussian Baths
summary: Gaussian baths are widely used to model non-Markovian environments, yet the cost of accurate simulation at long times remains poorly understood, especially when spectral densities exhibit nonanalytic behavior as in a range of realistic models. We rigorously bound the complexity of representing bath correlation functions on a time interval $[0,T]$ by sums of complex exponentials, as employed in recent variants of pseudomode and hierarchical equations of motion methods. These bounds make explicit the dependence on the maximal simulation time $T$, inverse temperature $β$, and the type and strength of singularities in an effective spectral density. For a broad class of spectral densities, the required number of exponentials is bounded independently of $T$, achieving time-uniform complexity. The $T$-dependence emerges only as polylogarithmic factors for spectral densities with strong singularities, such as step discontinuities and inverse power-law divergences. The temperature dependence is mild for bosonic environments and disappears entirely for fermionic environments. Thus, the true bottleneck for long-time simulation is not the simulation duration itself, but rather the presence of sharp nonanalytic features in the bath spectrum. Our results are instructive both for long-time simulation of non-Markovian open quantum systems, as well as for Markovian embeddings of classical generalized Langevin equations with memory kernels.

AI.tldr: The paper establishes rigorous complexity bounds for simulating Gaussian baths in non-Markovian open quantum systems, showing that the number of exponential terms needed to represent bath correlation functions is largely independent of simulation time T, with only polylogarithmic T-dependence for strongly singular spectral densities.
AI.motivation: To understand the computational cost of accurate long-time simulation of non-Markovian environments with Gaussian baths, particularly when spectral densities exhibit nonanalytic behavior common in realistic models, and to provide rigorous complexity bounds for methods like pseudomode and hierarchical equations of motion approaches.
AI.method: The authors develop rigorous mathematical bounds on the complexity of representing bath correlation functions as sums of complex exponentials. They analyze the dependence on simulation time T, inverse temperature β, and the type/strength of singularities in the effective spectral density, considering both bosonic and fermionic environments.
AI.result: For a broad class of spectral densities, the required number of exponentials is bounded independently of T (time-uniform complexity). T-dependence emerges only as polylogarithmic factors for spectral densities with strong singularities like step discontinuities and inverse power-law divergences. Temperature dependence is mild for bosonic environments and disappears entirely for fermionic environments.
AI.conclusion: The true bottleneck for long-time simulation of non-Markovian open quantum systems is not the simulation duration itself, but rather the presence of sharp nonanalytic features in the bath spectrum. These results provide fundamental complexity insights for both quantum system simulation and Markovian embeddings of classical generalized Langevin equations.
